Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 28, verses 29–31 (part 3 of 3):

* Among its lessons also: the refutation of the Jahmiyya and the Mu'tazila, who say that the speech of Allah is created. The proof for this is that it is established that the calling (nida') comes from whom? From Allah, glorified and exalted be He. And calling is a voice, a raised voice, and speech is not attributed except to a speaker, so the speech is the speech of Allah. Every attribute of Allah is uncreated, because it is a description of the one who is characterized by it; so when it is a description of the Creator, it is uncreated. Thus in the verse there is a refutation of the two groups: the Ash'ariyya and the Mu'tazila.
* Among its lessons also: that some places are blessed, but with a relative blessing (barakah idafiyya), not an absolute blessing, because of His saying: ﴿in the blessed valley﴾ [al-Qasas 30]. For whom is the blessing here?
* A student: For Musa.
* The Shaykh: For Musa (...), as the author said.
* Among its lessons also: the affirmation that the speech of Allah, glorified and exalted be He, consists of letters (bi-harf), from His saying: ﴿"O Musa, indeed I am Allah, the Lord of the worlds"﴾ [al-Qasas 30]. Indeed, ﴿"O Musa, indeed I am Allah, the Lord of the worlds"﴾ are sentences composed of letters, so in this there is a refutation of whom? The Ash'ariyya, because the Ash'ariyya say: speech is an inner meaning subsisting in the self. When I conceal (...), this concealed thing is the speech, and what is heard is not the speech but only an expression of it. There is no doubt that this is not valid. The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Allah has overlooked for my community what their souls whisper to them, so long as they do not act upon it or speak of it" [agreed upon; al-Bukhari (5269) and Muslim (127/201), from the hadith of Abu Hurayra, may Allah be pleased with him]. So he made clear that speech is other than the whispering of the soul.
* Among its lessons: the affirmation of the lordship of Allah, glorified and exalted be He, over everything, because of His saying: ﴿Indeed I am Allah, the Lord of the worlds﴾. What (...)?
What is the reconciliation between this verse and what comes in many verses of (...) lordship for some persons or (...) into two categories: general and specific, just as worship (ibadah) is also divided into two categories: general and specific. For example His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, My servants, you have no authority over them, except those who follow you of the deviators﴾ [al-Hijr 42]. Is this of the general or of the specific?
* A student: Of the general.
* The Shaykh: Because "My servants", "Indeed My servants, you have no authority over them, except those who follow you"...
* A student: General.
* The Shaykh: General? What is the evidence? The exception: ﴿except those who follow you of the deviators﴾. If we say the exception is disjunct (munqati'), ﴿Indeed My servants, you have no authority over them﴾ would be specific. But it is established that when it is uncertain whether the exception is connected (muttasil) or disjunct (munqati'), connection is preferable, so it is preferable that it be connected.
﴿There is none in the heavens and the earth but that he comes to the Most Merciful as a servant﴾ [Maryam 93]. General?
* A student: Yes.
* The Shaykh: ﴿And the servants of the Most Merciful are those who walk upon the earth in humility﴾ [al-Furqan 63]. This is specific.
﴿Indeed I am Allah, the Lord of the worlds (30). And cast your staff.' So when he saw it moving as if it were a snake, he turned back in flight and did not return﴾ [al-Qasas 30, 31].
* A student: (...).
* Another student: (...).
* The Shaykh: And His saying: ﴿And cast your staff﴾; ﴿so when he saw it moving﴾.
In this is evidence that Musa used to carry the staff, from His saying: ﴿cast your staff﴾.
And in it is evidence of the power of Allah, glorified and exalted be He, for by the mere moment he cast it, it became moving as if it were a snake, by the mere casting. In this is evidence of power (...). And in it is also evidence of the wisdom of Allah, glorified and exalted be He, since this verse is suited to those whom Musa will confront, for he will confront whom?
* A student: The magicians.
* The Shaykh: The magicians. This verse is entirely suitable for them, because they will be unable to match it (...).
* Among its lessons also: that this staff (...) is known for its swift movement, because it is a snake (jann).
* Among its lessons: that what is permissible for others is permissible for the prophets, namely natural fear, because of His saying: ﴿he turned back in flight and did not return﴾. Although Musa, as you know, was among the strong men, yet what befalls other human beings befell him, and it has already been mentioned that he left the city fearful, watchful.
* Among its lessons also: the care of Allah, exalted is He, for him, in that He called him and reassured him with His saying: ﴿Come forward and do not fear﴾ [al-Qasas 31]. He did not limit Himself to saying "do not fear," but asked him to come forward to Him: ﴿Come forward and do not fear﴾, and this indicates Allah's care for him and His love for him.
* Among its lessons also: that one who asks another to do something should state the reason for it, because of His saying: ﴿Indeed you are of the secure﴾ [al-Qasas 31]. For if He had said only "do not fear," the fear might depart from him, but he would not be completely reassured. When He said "Indeed you are of the secure," he increased in reassurance.
* Among its lessons also: that one should mention the like (nuzara') or allude to them, so that this is firmer for the heart, because of His saying: ﴿Indeed you are of the secure﴾.
(...)

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 28, verses 29–31 (part 1 of 3):

﴿So when Musa had fulfilled the term﴾ [al-Qasas: 29].
(Al) here is for definiteness, meaning: the term that was between him and the man of Madyan. We know that there were two terms between them: an obligatory term, which was eight years, and a voluntary term from Musa, which was ten years. Which of the two terms did he fulfil? Was it the obligatory one or the voluntary one?
The author, may Allah have mercy on him, says: (﴿So when Musa had fulfilled the term﴾ [al-Qasas: 29], which was eight or ten years, and it is the one thought of for him).
The pronoun in his saying "and it is the one thought of for him" refers to the ten years, meaning that it is supposed of Musa that he completed ten years. However, the verse admits of both possibilities. Preference for ten years is based on what is known of Musa's character, his generosity and fulfilment of promises (peace be upon him). Preference for eight years is because it was what was obligatory upon him. Musa was longing for his homeland in Egypt, and he had earlier said, apologising: ﴿Whichever of the two terms I fulfil, there shall be no injustice upon me﴾ [al-Qasas: 28]. This statement may indicate that he intended to limit himself to the obligatory term, for otherwise it is known that once he had fulfilled the first term, no one would blame or wrong him. So each view has its basis. Our stance regarding this story is to leave undetermined what Allah, the Glorified and Exalted, left undetermined, and to say: he fulfilled the term, and Allah knows best which of them he fulfilled.
﴿So when Musa had fulfilled the term and set out with his family﴾.
* Student: O Shaykh, what is narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, that Musa, peace be upon him, fulfilled (...)?
* Shaykh: Yes, it is narrated from Ibn 'Abbas and most of the exegetes (...), but there is nothing that favours it; each one (...).
* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: No (...). The correct view is that the exegesis of a Companion has no (...) absolutely, especially when it comes from Companions known for transmitting Isra'iliyyat, such as Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both.
His saying: ﴿and set out with his family﴾. Al-sayr (setting out) means walking. He set out with his family from the man of Madyan's place; he says: (his wife, with her father's permission, towards Egypt).
As for his saying "his wife", it is correct that a wife is called "family" (ahl). As for his saying "with her father's permission", there is no evidence for this, and a husband does not need his wife's father's permission when he wishes to travel with her. Why? Because once he marries the woman she becomes his possession, and he may take her wherever he wishes, except if he takes her toward something that is not permissible under the Shari'ah; then she may refuse, and her father may also prevent her, otherwise the right is his.
Now, what if it had been stipulated to him that he would not travel with her?
* Student: It binds him.
* Shaykh: Is fulfilment obligatory?
* Student: Yes.
* Shaykh: Yes, fulfilment is obligatory. But if she gave permission and her father refused, and it had been stipulated, is the right hers so that she travels, or her father's so that she does not? The right is hers. In truth the right is hers, because this concerns her personally, and she may see that it is better for her to travel with her husband.
(﴿ānasa﴾ [al-Qasas: 29]: saw from afar).
﴿ānasa﴾: the root of ﴿ānasa﴾ derives from intimacy (uns), which is the removal of fear, but it comes to mean catching sight of something, because when you see a thing and recognise it, what you feared departs from you. So the meaning of ﴿ānasa﴾ is "he saw".
﴿from the side of the Mount﴾ [al-Qasas: 29]: with a damma on the tur, it means a mountain. And the side (janib) of a thing, what does it mean?
* Student: Its edge.
* Shaykh: Its direction; that is, from the direction of the Tur. ﴿ānasa a fire﴾ [al-Qasas: 29]. This fire was not a real fire, but a light resembling fire. When he saw this fire, and it was the time of winter, and it is apparent, and Allah knows best, that the night was cloudy, and that Musa, peace be upon him, had some confusion about the way, as the story indicates.
He saw a fire, and then (﴿He said to his family: "Stay here"﴾ [al-Qasas: 29]).
﴿to his family: "Stay"﴾: the author's view a little earlier was that by "his family" is meant the wife, but here he said ﴿to his family: "Stay"﴾. Is "stay" addressed to a group or to one person?
* Student: To a group.
* Shaykh: Because if it were to one person he would have said "Stay" in the feminine singular. So it is addressed to a group. What is the way out of this difficulty if we say that "family" is only the wife?
Some exegetes said: he took with him a servant. Others also said: a child was born to him from her, based on the view that she was given to him from the beginning of the contract and remained with him for how many years? Eight or ten years, and she gave birth. On this view, the address ﴿Stay﴾ to a group corresponds to reality, yes, because with him are a wife, a servant and a child. Is that right or not? Because they are a group. This is not far-fetched, since it is customary that a person, when he travels, especially in such circumstances, takes with him someone to serve him.
And his saying: (﴿Stay﴾ here). From where do we take that "here" means in the place?
(A piece, and a brand ﴿from the fire, that you may warm yourselves﴾ [al-Qasas: 29])? (they warm themselves).
His saying: ﴿Perhaps I may bring you⁠﴾ [al-Qasas: 29]: is (la'alla) here for expectation or for hope?
* Student: For hope.
* Shaykh: For hope, because he wishes that this matter would come about for him.
﴿I may bring you from it news﴾ [al-Qasas: 29]: is (ātī) here a past verb or a present verb?
* Student: A present verb.
* Shaykh: A present verb: ﴿ātīkum﴾, and its origin is (a-ati-kum), meaning: I come to you.
Is it not an active participle (ātin)? Coming (al-ityān) is a verbal noun.
* Student: Yes.
* Shaykh: ﴿Indeed what you are promised is coming⁠﴾ [al-An'am: 134]. Here, can (ātī) not serve as an active participle?
No, it cannot, because here it intends the action; it does not intend to show that he is characterised by coming. The proof is that if you convert it to its meaning you would say: "Perhaps I may come to you," and "come" is clearly a present verb, so it is not an active participle here.
His saying: ﴿Perhaps I may bring you from it⁠﴾, that is, from this fire. It is known that the fire itself does not give news, but what is meant is from beside it, because a fire does not usually blaze except with people beside it.
His saying: ﴿news⁠﴾: the author says: (about the way, and he had gone astray). This is possible, and it could also be more general than being about the way: about the way, and about the remaining distance, and about anything at all. (Khabar, news) is indefinite.
His saying: ﴿or a burning brand from the fire﴾ [al-Qasas: 29]. The author says: (with three vowels on the jim). Recite it with the three vowels on the jim, recite it in the three ways.
* Student: bi-jidhwatin.
* Shaykh: Good.
* Student: And bi-jadhwa.
* Shaykh: Yes.
* Student: And bi-judhwa.
* Shaykh: (jidhwa, jadhwa, judhwa); this is the tathlith. When they say "muthallath" or "bi-tathlith", it means that the three vowel-patterns are permitted. But when they say "bi-l-muthallatha", this is different from "al-muthallath". What is the meaning of "al-muthallatha"?
* Student: The thā'.
* Shaykh: The thā', meaning it has three dots. So when it is said "bi-l-muthallatha", it means with the thā', not the tā'. When it is said "bi-tathlith such-and-such", the meaning is that the three vowels are permitted.
What is the jidhwa?
He said: (a piece and a brand ﴿from the fire﴾). That is, he brings a stick with a blazing fire at its end; this is the jidhwa.
His saying: ﴿from the fire, that you may warm yourselves⁠﴾ [al-Qasas: 29].
(La'alla) here is for causation, that is, so that you may warm yourselves. We have already passed that la'alla has several meanings: hope, apprehension, expectation, and causation. These are the meanings of la'alla.
He said: (﴿that you may warm yourselves﴾ means you seek warmth), because al-sali means seeking protection from the fire, so iṣṭilā' means seeking its protection, which is seeking warmth. This is evidence that they were in cold, is it not?
* Student: Yes.
* Shaykh: In cold.
He says: (the ṭā' replaces the tā' of the iftiʿāl). This is a morphological reason. What is the tā' of iftiʿāl? The one that indicates doing the act. (Iṣṭalā) originally is?
* Student: Iṣtalā.
* Shaykh: Iṣtalā, and ﴿taṣṭalūn⁠﴾ originally is (taṣtalūn), like tabtaghūn. But the morphological rule in Arabic is that when the tā' of iftiʿāl comes after a ṣād, it is changed to ṭā'. So one says (iṣṭalā) instead of (iṣtalā), and one says ﴿taṣṭalūn⁠﴾ instead of (taṣtalūn). From which is it derived? (From ṣaliya the fire, with a kasra or a fatha on the lam).
(With a kasra on the lam): ṣalia the fire, and with a fatha: ṣala the fire. So from (ṣaliya) like (raḍiya), or from (ṣala) like (ramā), and there are two dialects in Arabic. In the Qur'an: ﴿None will burn therein except the most wretched⁠﴾ [al-Layl: 15]. From which of the two patterns is it? From (raḍiya yarḍā) or from (ramā yarmī)?
* Student: (ramā yarmī).
* Shaykh: ﴿None will burn therein⁠﴾, from which of the two patterns?
* Student: From (raḍiya).
* Shaykh: From (raḍiya). If it were from (ramā) it would be lā yaṣlīhā, as one says lā yarmīhā.
So the Qur'an indicates what the author put forward, that the kasra on the lam is more eloquent, or not?
﴿He who will burn in the greatest fire⁠﴾ [al-A'la: 12]: ﴿yaṣlā⁠﴾, and he did not say yaṣlī, though it is permissible in Arabic.
The author, may Allah have mercy on him...
* Student: ṣalā bil-nār.
* Shaykh: Yes, one who ṣalā with the fire; I said: the fire.
﴿So when he came to it⁠﴾ [al-Qasas: 30].
* Student: O Shaykh, his saying in another surah: ﴿Perhaps I may bring you a burning brand from it, or find at the fire some guidance⁠﴾ [Ta-Ha: 10]; what does it mean here (...)?
* Shaykh: Unless... but if we say that the news is more general than that, its meaning is not that it negates this thing, and it indicates that he needed evidence. We said that it is also apparent that the sky was cloudy, otherwise he would have known the stars, since he was a shepherd and had remained eight years and knows most of the stars. But it is not far-fetched that the sky was cloudy.
His saying: ﴿So when he came to it, he was called⁠﴾ [al-Qasas: 30].
(When he came to it) means he came to the fire and reached it.
﴿He was called from the right side of the valley⁠﴾: ﴿nūdiya⁠﴾. Nida' is calling a person with a raised voice, and munajah is speaking privately with a lowered voice. Allah, the Exalted, has said: ﴿And We called him from the right side of the Mount and brought him near in secret conference⁠﴾ [Maryam: 52]. So Musa was called from a distance, then he drew near and was addressed in private.
His saying: ﴿He was called from the right side of the valley⁠﴾: is the word ﴿nūdiya⁠﴾ in the active or passive voice?
* Student: Passive.
* Shaykh: Passive. And who called him? Allah, as in another verse: ﴿When his Lord called to him in the sacred valley of Tuwa⁠﴾ [al-Nazi'at: 16]. Here the agent is omitted for what purpose?
* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: For its being known, because it is known that the one who called him was Allah, as in: ﴿Indeed, I am Allah, Lord of the worlds⁠﴾ [al-Qasas: 30].
His saying: (﴿from the right side⁠﴾ means the edge). The shati' of a thing is its edge, and from it is the shore of a river, the shore of a river meaning the bank of the river.
His saying: ﴿the valley⁠﴾: al-wadi is the course of water; the course of a thing is called a valley because it contains a gathering, and wadi means gathering, so the course of a thing is a valley.
His saying: ﴿from the right side of the valley⁠﴾: is the word ﴿al-ayman⁠﴾ an attribute of ﴿al-wadi⁠﴾ or an attribute of (al-shati')?
* Student: Of (al-shati').
* Shaykh: What is the evidence?
* Student: Because the valley has two sides.
* Shaykh: Yes, the valley has two sides, but we do not have two valleys, one right and one left. This is shown by His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And We made a covenant with you at the right side of the Mount⁠﴾ [Ta-Ha: 80].
So the word ﴿al-ayman⁠﴾ is an attribute of ﴿shati'⁠﴾, that is: from the right bank?
﴿al-ayman⁠﴾: the author says: (for Musa). It is known, because he was addressed; perhaps he was in front of a valley, or he was in the same valley, and the right of it is what is on his right, on Musa's right.
(﴿in the blessed ground⁠﴾ [al-Qasas: 30] for Musa). ﴿al-buq'a⁠﴾: what is the buq'a?
* Student: The land.
* Shaykh: Its origin: ﴿al-buq'a⁠﴾ [al-Qasas: 30] is a thing distinguished from others, as in the spots of water on a garment, for example. So buq'a means a part of the land that has a distinction, such as trees or the like.
His saying: ﴿al-mubaraka⁠﴾ means the one Allah, the Glorified and Exalted, has blessed, and baraka, as we have already passed, is abundant and enduring good.
* Student: Is the buq'a not the place without trees, O Shaykh?
* Shaykh: No, that is called the qa'.
* Student: With us they call it a buq'a, O Shaykh (...), meaning the place with no trees we say: this is a buq'a with no trees.
* Shaykh: Yes, no, that is called the qa'.
* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: Yes, with (...).
* Student: In the middle of the place (...).
* Shaykh: Yes, is it called?
* Student: A buq'a.
* Shaykh: No, that may be a customary usage of the language.
His saying: ﴿al-mubaraka⁠﴾ means the one in which Allah placed blessing, and baraka is abundant and enduring good, because it is derived from the pool of water (birka), and a pool of water is a gathering place for it together with its remaining in it. Baraka is from Allah, the Glorified and Exalted, and nothing is blessed in its own person, but for what Allah has placed in it of blessing. We have already passed a discussion about whether a person may seek blessing from another, such as when people say: "We visited you seeking blessing." Is this correct or not?
We said previously: if what is meant is personal blessing, this is not correct except for the Prophet ﷺ; but if what is meant by blessing is the benefit that results from him, whether knowledge or wealth, then this is correct, for some people's gatherings are blessed, benefiting those present, whether through remembrance, or knowledge, or wealth, or manners and ethics; this is blessing without doubt. And some people are the opposite, ill-omened to their companions, just as there are people who are a key to good and a lock against evil, and some are the reverse.
His saying: ﴿al-mubaraka⁠﴾ [al-Qasas: 30]. But the author restricted it with a good restriction, he said: (﴿al-mubaraka⁠﴾ for Musa). It is blessed at that time with respect to Musa; after that it has no religious character and is not sacred thereafter. We understand that this is specific to the time of Musa's being addressed.
Similarly, the Cave of Hira, for example: for the Messenger ﷺ it is blessed for the Messenger when? At the time the revelation descended upon him there. After that it has no religious character; therefore it is an innovation for a person to go to the Cave of Hira to visit it as an act of worship, and likewise the Cave of Thawr. But if he visits it only for sightseeing, there is no harm in it, since he does not intend worship. So, from these places that have no general sanctity, their sanctity is specific to when?
* Student: At that time.
* Shaykh: At that time only, and to the one for whom it was, and for others this ruling does not apply. Therefore, among the best things the author followed here is his restriction: (for Musa for his hearing the speech of Allah therein). For his hearing the speech of Allah in this place. There is no doubt that listening to the speech of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, is not like any other listening, because a person finds in it a delight of intimate conversation that he does not find in anyone else's conversation, because it is the most beloved thing to a person, and it is known that whenever a person addresses his beloved he becomes more delighted by his speech with him, though the speech of Allah is not like any speech.
(for his hearing the speech of Allah therein). Did he hear the speech of Allah from Allah, or from the tree?
* Student: From the tree.
* Shaykh: No, he heard it from Allah when He spoke it, and this is the doctrine of the People of the Sunnah and the Jama'ah. The Ash'aris differed, saying: the speech of Allah is the meaning subsisting in the self, and what is heard is a created thing that Allah created to express what is in the self. On this view, Musa did not hear the speech of Allah; he heard only what is an expression of the speech of Allah.
The Mu'tazila and the Jahmiyya also differed, and said: the speech of Allah is created; Allah, the Glorified and Exalted, creates sounds as He wills, either in Jibril, or in the tree, or in the earth, and these sounds are heard, and the speech is attributed to Allah by way of honour, creation and origination.

وعندما نُمحِّص الأمر، نجد أنه لا فرقَ بين الأشاعرة (al-Ash'ariyyah, the Ash'arites) والمعتزلة (al-Mu'tazilah, the Mu'tazilites) في هذا الباب، والسبب؛ لأن الكل مُتفقون على أن ما يُسْمَع فهو مخلوق، وليس هو كلام الله، ففي الحقيقة لا فرْق بينهما، لكن الأشاعرة تلطفوا في الأمر وقالوا: إن الكلام معنى قائم بالنفس يُعبَّر عنه بالأصوات، لا يُعبِّر المتكلم يَخلُق ما يَدُل عليه.

ولا ريب أن مذهب أهل السنة والجماعة (Ahl al-Sunnah wa al-Jama'ah, the People of the Sunnah and the Community) هو المذهب الصحيح الموافق للنقل والعقل (naql, transmitted texts, and 'aql, reason)، يقولون: إن كلام الله يُسمَع من الله، وإنه -أي كلام الله- بحرف وصوت، أما الحرف فهو ما يَتكلم به تبارك وتعالى مما يستعمله الناس في نُطقهم، في المخاطَبِين، وأما الصوت فإنه لا يشبه أصوات المخلوقين، وكيف يُشبه أصوات المخلوقين وهو سبحانه وتعالى إذا تكلم بوحي صعقتِ الملائكة وارتجفت السماوات ﴿حَتَّى إِذَا فُزِّعَ عَنْ قُلُوبِهِمْ قَالُوا مَاذَا قَالَ رَبُّكُمْ قَالُوا الْحَقَّ وَهُوَ الْعَلِيُّ الْكَبِيرُ﴾ [سبأ ٢٣].

قال: (﴿مِنَ الشَّجَرَةِ﴾ بَدَل مِنْ ﴿شَاطِئِ﴾ بِإِعَادَةِ الْجَار لِنَبَاتِهَا فِيهِ).

﴿نُودِيَ مِنْ شَاطِئِ الْوَادِ الْأَيْمَنِ فِي الْبُقْعَةِ الْمُبَارَكَةِ مِنَ الشَّجَرَةِ﴾ [القصص ٣٠]، يصير هنا تخصيص بعد تعميم، أو بعد تخصيص؟

فيه عندنا الآن تخصيص بالنسبة لجانب الشاطئ، ويش التخصيص فيه؟

* طالب: الأيمن.

* الشيخ: أنه الأيمن، وفيه أيضًا تخصيص ثانٍ بالنسبة للشاطئ، وهو أنه ﴿مِنَ الشَّجَرَةِ﴾، ﴿نُودِيَ﴾ ﴿مِنَ الشَّجَرَةِ﴾، أي: من ناحيتها، وليس معناه أن النداء من الشجرة، المعتزلة، يقولون: إن النداء من الشجرة، وإن الشجرة خُلِق فيها صوت سمعه موسى على أنه كلام الله. ولكن المراد ﴿مِنَ الشَّجَرَةِ﴾، أي: من ناحيتها وجِهَتِهَا، بدليل ما يأتي: ﴿إِنِّي أَنَا اللَّهُ رَبُّ الْعَالَمِينَ﴾ [القصص ٣٠] هل يمكن تقوله الشجرة؟

* طالب: لا.

* الشيخ: ما تقوله، ولو قالت الشجرةُ: ﴿إِنِّي أَنَا اللَّهُ رَبُّ الْعَالَمِينَ﴾، لقال لها موسى: كذبتِ. ولكن الذي يقول ذلك هو الله سبحانه وتعالى، وقوله: (لِنَبَاتِهَا فِيهِ وَهِيَ شَجَرَة عُنَّاب أَوْ عَلِيق) أو (عُلَيْق) ما أعرف ضبطها (أَوْ عَوْسَج).

(أو) هذه لتنويع الخلاف، ولكن نحن لا يهمنا أن تكون هذا أو هذا، المهم أنها شجرة نُودِي منها عليه الصلاة والسلام (peace be upon him).

والنداء: (﴿أَنْ﴾ مُفَسِّرَة لَا مخففة ﴿يَا مُوسَى إِنِّي أَنَا اللَّهُ رَبُّ الْعَالَمِينَ﴾ ).

(﴿أَنْ﴾ [القصص ٣٠] مفسرة) والمفسرة هي التي بمعنى (أي)، وهي التي تأتي مُفَسِّرة لما فيه معنى القول دون حروفه. (مفسرة) بمعنى أيش؟

* طالب: (أي).

* الشيخ: بمعنى (أي)، وهي التي تأتي مفسرة لما فيه معني القول دون حروفه. ويش معنى (لما فيه معنى القول دون حروفه)؟ يعني: بكلمة فيها معنى القول لا حروف القول. النداء فيه معنى القول ولَّا حروفه؟

* طالب: معناه.

* الشيخ: معناه، ما فيها: (قيل له)، بل فيها نون، فتكون مُفسِّرة.

﴿فَأَوْحَيْنَا إِلَيْهِ أَنِ اصْنَعِ الْفُلْكَ﴾ [المؤمنون ٢٧].

﴿فَأَوْحَيْنَا إِلَيْهِ أَنِ اصْنَعِ﴾، (أَنْ) هذه مُفَسِّرة ولَّا مخففة؟

* طالب: مُفَسِّرة.

* الشيخ: مفسرة؛ لأنها أتت لما فيه معنى القول -وهو الإيحاء- دون حروف القول، وقول المؤلف..

* طالب: كيف يا شيخ دون الحروف؟

* الشيخ: يعني دون حروف القول، القول اللي هو (قاف، واو، لام).

* الطالب: يعني (...)؟

* الشيخ: لا، معناه أنها تكون مُفسِّرة لفعلٍ فيه معنى القول لا حروف القول، يعني مثلًا لو قال: قيل له: ﴿أَنْ يَا مُوسَى﴾، ما تكون في معنى المفسرة؛ لأن فيها حروف القول، لكن ﴿نُودِيَ﴾ تكون ﴿أَنْ﴾ مفسرة؛ لأن فيها معنى القول؛ ولهذا سميناها مُفسِّرة؛ لأنها فَسَّرَت النداء بالقول، إذ إن مدخولها: ﴿أَنْ يَا مُوسَى إِنِّي أَنَا اللَّهُ﴾ [القصص ٣٠]، مدخولها قول ولَّا لا؟ قول، ﴿يَا مُوسَى إِنِّي أَنَا اللَّهُ﴾ هذا قول، فلهذا نقول: إنها (مفسرة)؛ لأنها فسرت معنى الفعل حيث تضمن القولَ دون حروف القول.

وقوله: (لا مخفَّفة)، (مخففة) منين؟

* طالب: من الثقيلة.

* الشيخ: من الثقيلة، فلا تصِح أن تكون مخففة؛ لأنه ينطبق عليها معنى التفسيرية؛ هذه واحدة، وأيضًا الْمُخَفَّفَة تحتاج إلى تقدير، أيش اللي بيقدر؟

* طالب: ضمير الشأن.

* الشيخ: يُقدر اسم اللي هو ضمير الشأن، والأصل.

* طالب: عدمه.

* الشيخ: عدم التقدير.

وقول المؤلف: (لا مخففة) أشار إلى نفيه؛ لأن بعض المعرضين يقولون: إنها مخففة.

﴿يَا مُوسَى إِنِّي أَنَا اللَّهُ رَبُّ الْعَالَمِينَ﴾ [القصص ٣٠].

﴿إِنِّي أَنَا اللَّهُ﴾، يعني الذي أخاطبك، ﴿أَنَا اللَّهُ﴾ فبدأ بالألوهية؛ لأنها هي المقصود.

وقال: ﴿رَبُّ الْعَالَمِينَ﴾، ثنَّى بالربوبية؛ لأن الربوبية في الحقيقة وسيلة إلى الألوهية؛ ولهذا مَن أقرَّ بالربوبية لزِمه أن يُقِر بالألوهية، وإلا كان متناقضًا، والله تعالى يحتج على المشركين بالألوهية، يَحتج عليهم دائمًا بإقرارهم بالربوبية؛ لأن من أقر أن الله ربُّه فإنه يقال له: إذن يجب أن تعبد هذا الرب، إذَا عبدتَ معه غيره فإنك لم تَصدُق بإقرارك بربوبيته، فهما متلازمان؛ ولهذا قال الله سبحانه وتعالى: ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ اعْبُدُوا رَبَّكُمُ الَّذِي خَلَقَكُمْ وَالَّذِينَ مِنْ قَبْلِكُمْ﴾ [البقرة ٢١]، فجعل الخَلْق الذي هو مِن مقتضى الربوبية دليلًا مُلزمًا لعبادته، ﴿اعْبُدُوا رَبَّكُمُ الَّذِي خَلَقَكُمْ﴾.

﴿إِنِّي أَنَا اللَّهُ﴾، ماذا تعربون ﴿أَنَا﴾؟

* طالب: خبر المبتدأ.

* الشيخ: خبر المبتدأ؟! ما يمكن الضمير يصير خبرًا أبدًا.

* طالب: بدل من الضمير.

* الشيخ: بدل؟

* الطالب: من (...).

* الشيخ: لا، تصح ضمير فصل؟

* طالب: نعم، فصل.

* الشيخ: ضمير الفصل يفصل بين الخبر والصفة، وهذا ما يعنيه، لو قال: (إني اللهُ) لاشتبه الأمر، فالظاهر لي أنها مبتدأ: ﴿إِنِّي﴾ أي المتكلم ﴿أَنَا اللَّهُ﴾ [القصص ٣٠]، كما قال: ﴿إِنَّنِي أَنَا اللَّهُ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا أَنَا﴾ [طه ١٤]، فهي مبتدأ و﴿اللَّهُ﴾ [القصص ٣٠] خبره، وجملة المبتدأ والخبر في محل رفع خبر (إن).

وقوله: ﴿رَبُّ الْعَالَمِينَ﴾ [القصص ٣٠] خبرٌ ثان لـ﴿أَنَا﴾.

و﴿رَبُّ الْعَالَمِينَ﴾ ما معنى الرب؟ هو الخالق.

* طالب: الخالق المدبِّر.

* الشيخ: المالِك المُدَبِّر لجميع الأشياء.

وقوله: ﴿الْعَالَمِينَ﴾ [القصص ٣٠] الْمُراد بهم مَن سوى الله، وجَمعَهم باعتبار أصنافهم، وإلا فالعالَم: كلُّ ما سوى الله فهو عالَم، لكن جُمعوا (عالَمين)؛ لأنه فيه مثلًا عالَم الإنس، عالَم الجن، عالَم البهائم، عالَم الملائكة، فجُمعوا باعتبار أجناسهم.

وهذه الربوبية عامة ولَّا خاصة؟ عامة، وقد مر علينا أن الربوبية تنقسم إلى عامة وخاصة، كما أن العبادة أو العُبودية تنقسم إلى عامة وخاصة، وقد اجتمعا في قوله تعالى: ﴿قَالُوا آمَنَّا بِرَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ (٤٧) رَبِّ مُوسَى وَهَارُونَ﴾ [الشعراء ٤٧، ٤٨]. فقوله: ﴿بِرَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ﴾ هذه العامة، و﴿رَبِّ مُوسَى وَهَارُونَ﴾ خاصة.

* طالب: في آية أخرى: ﴿إِنِّي أَنَا رَبُّكَ فَاخْلَعْ﴾ [طه ١٢]؟

* الشيخ: إي نعم، نحن نتكلم عن مثل الآية هذه ﴿إِنِّي أَنَا اللَّهُ رَبُّ الْعَالَمِينَ﴾ [القصص ٣٠].

﴿وَأَنْ أَلْقِ عَصَاكَ﴾ [القصص ٣١].

* طالب: شيخ، ذكرت أنه في مذهب أهل السنة والجماعة أن الله يتكلم بحرف وصوت.

* الشيخ: نعم.

* الطالب: وأن الحرف من جنس الحروف التي يستعملها الناس.

* الشيخ: التي يتكلم بها الناس.

* الطالب: ما يقتضي هذا التشبيه؟

* الشيخ: لا، لا يقتضي التشبيه؛ لأن الحروف هذه ما هي بصفة لله، صفةُ الله الصوت، أما الحروف فإنها منطوق بها وليست نطقًا، ما فيها تشبيه.

* الطالب: فائدة ذكر الشجرة: ﴿مِنَ الشَّجَرَةِ﴾ [القصص ٣٠]؟

* الشيخ: فائدة ذكر ﴿مِنَ الشَّجَرَةِ﴾ يعني معناه تحديد المكان، المقصود تحديد المكان؛ لأن ﴿شَاطِئِ الْوَادِ﴾ [القصص ٣٠] واسع وعام، فتخصيص المكان هذا يكون أبيَن؛ إذ إن موسى لو نُودي من جميع الشاطئ لالتبس عليه الأمر، لكن إذا حُدِّد النِّداء من جهة معينة خاصة صار هذا أبين له وأوضح.

قال: ﴿وَأَنْ أَلْقِ عَصَاكَ﴾ [القصص ٣١]، هذه معطوفة على قوله: ﴿أَنْ يَا مُوسَى﴾ [القصص ٣٠]، ﴿نُودِيَ﴾ ﴿أَنْ يَا مُوسَى﴾، يعني: ونودي أيضًا أن ﴿أَلْقِ عَصَاكَ﴾، و﴿أَلْقِ﴾ بمعنى: ضَعْ عصاك على الأرض، و﴿عَصَاكَ﴾ لماذا استصحبها؟

* طالب: للرعي.

* الشيخ: إي، ويش قال؟

* الطالب: ﴿أَتَوَكَّأُ﴾ عليها.

* الشيخ: ﴿أَتَوَكَّأُ عَلَيْهَا وَأَهُشُّ بِهَا عَلَى غَنَمِي وَلِيَ فِيهَا مَآرِبُ أُخْرَى﴾ [طه ١٨]، ﴿مَآرِبُ أُخْرَى﴾ ما ذَكَرها، ويش هي المآرب الأخرى؟

* الطالب: قيل: إنه (...)، والله أعلم.

* الشيخ: إي نعم، وغير؟

* الطالب: ويدفع بها السباع.

* الشيخ: إي، ويدفع بها السباع ويدفع بها عن نفسه، لكن ذكَر جانب المصالح: ﴿أَتَوَكَّأُ عَلَيْهَا وَأَهُشُّ بِهَا عَلَى غَنَمِي﴾، وأما جانب دفع المفاسد فأجمله في قوله: ﴿وَلِيَ فِيهَا مَآرِبُ أُخْرَى﴾، وهذا في الحقيقة من الأدب في النطق، وتجدون أن صفات الله سبحانه وتعالى في مقام الإثبات يُؤتى فيها بالتفصيل، وفي مقام النفي يُؤتى فيها بالإجمال غالبًا.

قال: (﴿وَأَنْ أَلْقِ عَصَاكَ﴾ فَأَلْقَاهَا ﴿فَلَمَّا رَآهَا تَهْتَزُّ﴾ تَتَحَرَّك ﴿كَأَنَّهَا جَانٌّ﴾ وَهِيَ الْحَيَّة الصَّغِيرَة مِنْ سُرْعَة حَرَكَتهَا) هذا وجْه التشبيه (﴿وَلَّى مُدْبِرًا﴾ [القصص ٣١] هَارِبًا مِنْهَا).

قوله: ﴿فَلَمَّا رَآهَا﴾ أبصرَها، وعلى هذا فيكون جملة ﴿تَهْتَزُّ﴾ في موضع نصبٍ على الحال، وليست مفعولًا ثانيًا؛ لأن (رأى) البَصَرية ما تنصب إلا مفعولًا واحدًا. أين جواب (لَمَّا) ﴿فَلَمَّا رَآهَا تَهْتَزُّ﴾؟

* طالب: ﴿وَلَّى﴾.

* الشيخ: ﴿وَلَّى مُدْبِرًا﴾.

وقوله: ﴿تَهْتَزُّ﴾، يقول: (تتحرك)، تتحرك لكنْ باهتزاز، نوع من الاضطراب، وتعرفون أن الحية تتحرك يمينًا وشمالًا.

وقوله: ﴿كَأَنَّهَا جَانٌّ﴾ هذا للتشبيه، يعني كأنها في هيئتها وفي حركتها؛ يعني في ذاتها وفي حركتها ﴿جَانٌّ﴾ قال: (وَهِيَ الْحَيَّة الصَّغِيرَة) هذا الجان. ووجه المشابهة؟

* طالب: الحركة.

* الشيخ: الحركة، سرعة الحركة، ولكن المؤلف فسَّر الجانَّ بأنها الحية الصغيرة، والله تعالى يقول في آية أخرى: ﴿فَأَلْقَى عَصَاهُ فَإِذَا هِيَ﴾ [الأعراف ١٠٧].

* طالب: ﴿حَيَّةٌ تَسْعَى﴾ [طه ٢٠].

* الشيخ: ﴿ثُعْبَانٌ مُبِينٌ﴾ [الأعراف ١٠٧]، ﴿ثُعْبَانٌ﴾، والثعبان: الذَّكَر من الحيات الكبيرة. فما الجمع بينهما؟

قالوا: إن الجمع بينهما أنه أول ما ألقاها صارت كالجان، ثم بعد ذلك تضخمت حتى كانت ثعبانًا مبينًا، حتى صارت ثعبانًا مبينًا.

* طالب: (...).

* الشيخ: إي نعم، عند السحرة.

(﴿كَأَنَّهَا جَانٌّ وَلَّى مُدْبِرًا﴾ [القصص ٣١] هَارِبًا مِنْهَا)، و﴿مُدْبِرًا﴾ هذه حال، ويُسمونها: حال مؤكِّدة، أيش معنى مؤكِّدة؟ لأن التولي معناه الإدبار، فهي حال مُؤَكِّدة لعاملها؛ إذ إن معنى الإدبار مفهومٌ من قوله: ﴿وَلَّى﴾، ولكنها جاءت للتأكيد، وقوله: ﴿مُدْبِرًا﴾ يعني ولَّاها دبره؛ ولهذا قال المؤلف: (هاربًا)؛ لأن الهارب ما يمشي إلى جنب، وإنما يمشي على العكس، عندما تهرب، أولًا: عندما تنصرف عن الشيء تُسمى مُوَلِّيًا، لكن إذا كنت هاربًا هل تُوَلِّي جنبك وتمشي مثلًا باتجاهٍ مُجانِب أو باتجاه معاكِس؟ باتجاه معاكس؛ ولهذا قال: (﴿وَلَمْ يُعَقِّبْ﴾ [القصص ٣١] أي يرجع)، معناه أنه هرب.

ولكن الله يقول: ﴿وَلَمْ يُعَقِّبْ﴾، يقول المؤلف: (فنودي ﴿يَا مُوسَى أَقْبِلْ وَلَا تَخَفْ﴾ [القصص ٣١])، ولهذا ينبغي أن نقف على قوله: ﴿وَلَمْ يُعَقِّبْ﴾؛ لأنه لو وصَلنا ﴿وَلَمْ يُعَقِّبْ يَا مُوسَى﴾ لظَنَّ الظانُّ أن الكلام واحد، ولكن الكلام انفصل، فقال: ﴿يَا مُوسَى أَقْبِلْ وَلَا تَخَفْ إِنَّكَ مِنَ الْآمِنِينَ﴾.

﴿أَقْبِلْ﴾ مقابل (التولِّي)، ﴿وَلَا تَخَفْ﴾ مقابل (الهرب)؛ لأن الهارب يكون خائفًا.

ثم طمأنه بقوله: ﴿إِنَّكَ مِنَ الْآمِنِينَ﴾، تأكيدًا لقوله: ﴿وَلَا تَخَفْ﴾؛ لأن الآمِن ما يخاف، وإنما يخاف مَن ليس عنده أمْن.

وهنا قال: ﴿إِنَّكَ مِنَ الْآمِنِينَ﴾، ولم يقل: إنك آمِن، بل قال: ﴿مِنَ الْآمِنِينَ﴾، فما هو البلاغة في هذا؟

* طالب: مراعاة القوافي.

* الشيخ: نعم، مراعاة الفواصل، يمكن نقول هذا: مراعاة الفواصل، لكنَّ هذه المناسبة لفظية.

* الطالب: لنعلم أنها (...).

* الشيخ: نعم، ليتذكَّر أن هناك آمِنين، فإذا كان هناك آمنون فإنه لا غرابة أن تأْمَن؛ لأن الإنسان إذا ذُكِّر بما حدَث لغيره صار أشد طمأنينة في حصول ذلك الشيء. ونظيره بالعكس قول فرعون: ﴿لَئِنِ اتَّخَذْتَ إِلَهًا غَيْرِي لَأَجْعَلَنَّكَ مِنَ الْمَسْجُونِينَ﴾ [الشعراء ٢٩]، ولم يقل: لأسْجُنَنَّك؛ لأجل أن يُرهبه بأن عنده مَنْ هو مسجون، وأنه ليس يُعجزُنا أن نسجنَك. فالحاصل أن مثل هذا يُقال لأجل أن يتذكر موسى عليه الصلاة والسلام أن هناك أناسًا آمنين، فيأمن أكثر. (...)

حيث إن الإنسان يعلم أن الله سبحانه وتعالى حكيم جعل لكل شيء سببًا، فيأخذ بهذه الأسباب (...).

ثم بُعث (...)، لماذا؟

* طالب: (...).

* الشيخ: إي، لأنه (...). كذلك إذا أراد أن يخرج خارج البلد فإنه ينبغي (...)؛ لأن الأمور (...)، وربما تحدث أشياء تحتاج إلى (...)، فهذه الأشياء ينبغي للإنسان أن (...).

* طالب: (...).

* الشيخ:* ومنها أيضًا: أن اتخاذ الأسباب لا ينافي التوكل (...) اتخاذ الإنسان للأسباب لا ينافي التوكل، بل هو من تمام التوكل، ومن تمام معرفة الإنسان لله سبحانه وتعالى، حيث إن الإنسان يعلم أن الله سبحانه وتعالى حكيم، جعل لكل شيء سببًا، فيأخذ بهذه الأسباب (...). لكن المحظور الذي ينافي التوكل هو أن الإنسان يعتمد على السبب، لا (...)، هذا من المحظور، وأما أن يأخذ بالسبب عارفًا بذلك (...).

ثم قال تعالى: ﴿فَلَمَّا أَتَاهَا نُودِيَ مِنْ شَاطِئِ الْوَادِ الْأَيْمَنِ فِي الْبُقْعَةِ الْمُبَارَكَةِ مِنَ الشَّجَرَةِ أَنْ يَا مُوسَى إِنِّي أَنَا اللَّهُ رَبُّ الْعَالَمِينَ﴾ [القصص ٣٠].

* في هذه الآية: إثبات الكلام لله سبحانه وتعالى؛ لأن ﴿نُودِيَ﴾ [القصص ٣٠] المُنادِي مَنْ؟ هو الله؛ لقوله تعالى في آية أخرى: ﴿إِذْ نَادَاهُ رَبُّهُ بِالْوَادِ الْمُقَدَّسِ طُوًى﴾ [النازعات ١٦].

* ومِنها: أن كلام الله تعالى بصوت؛ لقوله: ﴿نُودِيَ﴾، والنداء يكون بِصَوْت للبعيد، والمناجاة بصوت لمن؟ للقريب.

* ومنها: الرد على الأشاعرة الذين يقولون: إنَّ كلام الله هو المعنى القائم بنفسِه. ولا شك أن المعنى القائم بالنفس لا يسمى كلامًا ولا يُسمَع، وكلام الله تعالى يُسْمَع.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 28, verses 29–31 (part 3 of 3):

* Among its lessons also: the refutation of the Jahmiyya and the Mu'tazila, who say that the speech of Allah is created. The proof for this is that it is established that the calling (nida') comes from whom? From Allah, glorified and exalted be He. And calling is a voice, a raised voice, and speech is not attributed except to a speaker, so the speech is the speech of Allah. Every attribute of Allah is uncreated, because it is a description of the one who is characterized by it; so when it is a description of the Creator, it is uncreated. Thus in the verse there is a refutation of the two groups: the Ash'ariyya and the Mu'tazila.
* Among its lessons also: that some places are blessed, but with a relative blessing (barakah idafiyya), not an absolute blessing, because of His saying: ﴿in the blessed valley﴾ [al-Qasas 30]. For whom is the blessing here?
* A student: For Musa.
* The Shaykh: For Musa (...), as the author said.
* Among its lessons also: the affirmation that the speech of Allah, glorified and exalted be He, consists of letters (bi-harf), from His saying: ﴿"O Musa, indeed I am Allah, the Lord of the worlds"﴾ [al-Qasas 30]. Indeed, ﴿"O Musa, indeed I am Allah, the Lord of the worlds"﴾ are sentences composed of letters, so in this there is a refutation of whom? The Ash'ariyya, because the Ash'ariyya say: speech is an inner meaning subsisting in the self. When I conceal (...), this concealed thing is the speech, and what is heard is not the speech but only an expression of it. There is no doubt that this is not valid. The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Allah has overlooked for my community what their souls whisper to them, so long as they do not act upon it or speak of it" [agreed upon; al-Bukhari (5269) and Muslim (127/201), from the hadith of Abu Hurayra, may Allah be pleased with him]. So he made clear that speech is other than the whispering of the soul.
* Among its lessons: the affirmation of the lordship of Allah, glorified and exalted be He, over everything, because of His saying: ﴿Indeed I am Allah, the Lord of the worlds﴾. What (...)?
What is the reconciliation between this verse and what comes in many verses of (...) lordship for some persons or (...) into two categories: general and specific, just as worship (ibadah) is also divided into two categories: general and specific. For example His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, My servants, you have no authority over them, except those who follow you of the deviators﴾ [al-Hijr 42]. Is this of the general or of the specific?
* A student: Of the general.
* The Shaykh: Because "My servants", "Indeed My servants, you have no authority over them, except those who follow you"...
* A student: General.
* The Shaykh: General? What is the evidence? The exception: ﴿except those who follow you of the deviators﴾. If we say the exception is disjunct (munqati'), ﴿Indeed My servants, you have no authority over them﴾ would be specific. But it is established that when it is uncertain whether the exception is connected (muttasil) or disjunct (munqati'), connection is preferable, so it is preferable that it be connected.
﴿There is none in the heavens and the earth but that he comes to the Most Merciful as a servant﴾ [Maryam 93]. General?
* A student: Yes.
* The Shaykh: ﴿And the servants of the Most Merciful are those who walk upon the earth in humility﴾ [al-Furqan 63]. This is specific.
﴿Indeed I am Allah, the Lord of the worlds (30). And cast your staff.' So when he saw it moving as if it were a snake, he turned back in flight and did not return﴾ [al-Qasas 30, 31].
* A student: (...).
* Another student: (...).
* The Shaykh: And His saying: ﴿And cast your staff﴾; ﴿so when he saw it moving﴾.
In this is evidence that Musa used to carry the staff, from His saying: ﴿cast your staff﴾.
And in it is evidence of the power of Allah, glorified and exalted be He, for by the mere moment he cast it, it became moving as if it were a snake, by the mere casting. In this is evidence of power (...). And in it is also evidence of the wisdom of Allah, glorified and exalted be He, since this verse is suited to those whom Musa will confront, for he will confront whom?
* A student: The magicians.
* The Shaykh: The magicians. This verse is entirely suitable for them, because they will be unable to match it (...).
* Among its lessons also: that this staff (...) is known for its swift movement, because it is a snake (jann).
* Among its lessons: that what is permissible for others is permissible for the prophets, namely natural fear, because of His saying: ﴿he turned back in flight and did not return﴾. Although Musa, as you know, was among the strong men, yet what befalls other human beings befell him, and it has already been mentioned that he left the city fearful, watchful.
* Among its lessons also: the care of Allah, exalted is He, for him, in that He called him and reassured him with His saying: ﴿Come forward and do not fear﴾ [al-Qasas 31]. He did not limit Himself to saying "do not fear," but asked him to come forward to Him: ﴿Come forward and do not fear﴾, and this indicates Allah's care for him and His love for him.
* Among its lessons also: that one who asks another to do something should state the reason for it, because of His saying: ﴿Indeed you are of the secure﴾ [al-Qasas 31]. For if He had said only "do not fear," the fear might depart from him, but he would not be completely reassured. When He said "Indeed you are of the secure," he increased in reassurance.
* Among its lessons also: that one should mention the like (nuzara') or allude to them, so that this is firmer for the heart, because of His saying: ﴿Indeed you are of the secure﴾.
(...)

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 28, verse 32 (part 1 of 2):

He said: ﴿Insert your hand into your bosom﴾ [al-Qasas 32].
The author said: (﴿usluk﴾ means insert (adkhil), ﴿yadaka﴾ means the right hand, in the sense of the palm, ﴿fi jaybika﴾).
His words, ﴿usluk﴾, mean: insert (adkhil), so the meaning of ﴿usluk﴾ is: insert.
As for his words, (﴿yadaka﴾ means the palm), in reality there is no need for this, because (...). Rather, the word "yad" (hand), when used without qualification, means the palm. This is why, when Allah the Exalted said, ﴿As for the thief, male and female, cut off their hands (aydiyahuma)﴾ [al-Ma'idah 38], they said: the meaning of "aydi" is the palms (akuf). But if "yad" is intended to mean something other than the palm, it is qualified by it, as in the words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿wash your faces and your hands (aydiyakum) up to the elbows﴾ [al-Ma'idah 6]. In tayammum He said: ﴿wipe your faces and your hands (aydikum) with it﴾ [al-Ma'idah 6], and the difference is wiping only the palm, that is, not all of it. So "yad" when used without qualification means only the palm.
As for his words (the right, al-yumna), from where do we take it? There is no evidence in the verse for this. For this reason it is better for us to leave it unspecified, as Allah the Exalted left it unspecified, and it does not concern us whether it is the right hand or the left hand. What matters is that it was said: ﴿into your bosom﴾ [al-Qasas 32] is the collar (tawq) of the shirt, and bring it out.
His words, (it is the collar of the shirt) (...), through which the head enters. So the jayb is the collar through which the head enters the shirt.
His words, (and bring it out, ﴿takhruj﴾ [al-Qasas 32]), the author estimated a command in order to fit the answer, because it is not merely insertion so that it comes out white; rather, when he brings it out, it comes out white. But in reality there is no need for that, and there is no objection to ﴿takhruj﴾ being an answer to his words ﴿usluk﴾; for when you say "insert", the consequence is that he brought it out, and the original state is that nothing is omitted. Accordingly, ﴿takhruj﴾ here is in the jussive mood as an answer to the imperative in ﴿usluk﴾, because when the fa' is omitted from the answer of an imperative it becomes jussive, and when the fa' is present with it, it becomes subjunctive with (an). Ibn Malik said:
"After the fa' of an answer to a negation or a pure command, (an) puts it in the subjunctive, and its concealment is obligatory."
Meaning: (an) puts the verb in the subjunctive after the fa' that comes as an answer to a negation or a pure command; but if the fa' is dropped, the verb is put in the jussive. And he says:
"The condition for jussiveness after a prohibition is that you place (in) before (la), without a contradiction arising."
Here it is in the sense of a command, a command in the imperative.
(﴿takhruj﴾ contrary to what it was of the adma).
(The adma) is the swarthiness; that is, the color between white and black is called adma, and Musa ﷺ was adam (of swarthy complexion).
So he inserted his hand, and it came out ﴿white, without any defect﴾ [al-Qasas 32], that is, without any blemish, and a blemish distresses a person. And what is the whiteness that distresses a person? It is leprosy (baras), and for this reason the author said: (that is, leprosy).
As for his words ﴿white (bayda')﴾, what is its grammatical position?
* Student: A circumstantial clause (hal).
* The Shaykh: A hal from whom? From the subject of ﴿takhruj﴾.
﴿white, without any defect﴾. He said: (So he inserted it and brought it out, shining like the rays of the sun, dazzling the sight).
This is exaggeration. It is enough for us to say: Allah the Exalted did not say ﴿white, without any defect﴾ except to mean it is not leprosy, but whiteness without (...). As for it shining, Allah would have said: it comes out luminous, because luminosity is more emphatic than mere whiteness. Likewise, it is also stronger for the verse, and we say as Allah said: ﴿bayda'﴾.
(﴿And draw your arm close to your side against fear (al-rahb)﴾ [al-Qasas 32], with the two letters vocalized as fatha) ﴿al-rahab﴾.
(And the second letter quiescent with the first letter fatha or damma) (the second letter quiescent) meaning the ha', (with the first letter fatha), which is the ra', (or damma). So the readings are three: ﴿al-rahab﴾, ﴿al-rahb﴾, and ﴿al-ruhb﴾.
So ﴿And draw your arm close to your side from the rahab﴾ is correct, right?
* Student: Yes.
* The Shaykh: Correct, it is the reading with which the author began.
﴿And draw your arm close to your side from the ruhb﴾ [al-Qasas 32] is correct.
﴿And draw your arm close to your side from the rahb﴾ is also correct.
His words ﴿your arm (janahaka)﴾: the intended meaning of "janah" is the hand, because for a person it is like the wing for a bird.
His words ﴿from fear (min al-rahb)﴾: ﴿min﴾ is causal; its meaning is causality. As for grammar, it is the particle of genitive.
He said: (that is, fear). This is an explanation of ﴿al-rahb﴾; ﴿al-rahb﴾ means fear.
The author's meaning: (that is, the fear arising from the shining of the hand, by inserting it into your bosom, so that it returns to its first state).
That is, if he says ﴿white, without any defect﴾, and you want it to return to its former state, then draw it to your side a second time, and then it returns to its state. If he inserts it into his bosom and brings it out, it becomes white, and if he wants it to return to its state, he draws it to himself and it returns to its state. This is the meaning of the author's statement.
Some scholars said: this sentence is separate from the first sentence, because Allah the Exalted guided him, if he feared, to place his hand on his chest until the fear leaves him. Is this sign for Musa alone, that whenever he fears something he places his hand on his chest, or is it general for everyone?
In any case, with regard to Musa, (...) that when he fears Pharaoh or anyone else, he draws his hand to himself. But others: it was narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, that he said: No one who is seized by terror after Musa places his hand on his chest and draws it in, except that the terror leaves him.[[Abu Muhammad al-Qayrawani mentioned in his tafsir al-Hidayah ila Bulugh al-Nihayah (8/5530) from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: No one is seized by terror after Musa, then inserts his hand and draws it to his chest, except that the terror departs from him.]]
(...)
In any case, with regard to Musa, there are now two opinions among the scholars:
The first opinion: this is a treatment to restore the hand to its former state. This is weakened by the fact that Allah said: ﴿And draw your arm close to your side from the rahb﴾, and Musa had not feared, since Allah had said to him: ﴿white, without any defect﴾, so he did not fear.
The second opinion: when fear arises in Musa, as you know from the verse, ﴿he turned back fleeing﴾ [al-Qasas 31] in fear, so Allah guided him that if he wanted to remove the fear from (...), he should draw his hand to himself, to his own self: ﴿And draw your arm close to your side from the rahb﴾ [al-Qasas 32].
(And he expressed it by the wing, because for a person it is like the wing for a bird), and this is correct; it is also a wing. Even a person, when he rises (...) with his hands, does he not? Yes indeed; if you tie his hands, he cannot (...). Without doubt, they help a person just as a bird's wing helps it.
(﴿Fadhanika﴾ [al-Qasas 32] with shaddah and without shaddah; that is, the staff and the hand, and both are feminine, and the demonstrative referring to them was made masculine to agree with its predicate).
* Student: (...)?
* The Shaykh: Yes, (...); because the two hands, as you know, one is a wing and the other (...). When he inserts it into his bosom (...), and this is what prevents saying (...), whether in the Arabic language or in the Qur'an.
His words ﴿fadhanika﴾, he says: (with shaddah and without shaddah).
(With shaddah): ﴿fadhanika﴾ with the nun doubled, and (without shaddah): ﴿fadhaka﴾.
We want someone to cite for us from the words of Ibn Malik for these two readings, shaddah and no shaddah.
* Student: (...).
* The Shaykh: (...).
"And the nun in dhayn and tayn is also doubled..."
For example: the nun in al-ladhan and al-latan.
"...and compensation by that is intended."
("Fadhanika" with shaddah and without shaddah; that is, the staff and the hand), ("the staff") is feminine or masculine?
* Student: Feminine.
* The Shaykh: Feminine. He said: ﴿It is my staff; I lean upon it﴾ [Ta-Ha 18], and did not say "he is my staff, I lean upon him," but said ﴿it is my staff, I lean upon it﴾. Is "the hand" masculine or feminine?
* Student: Masculine.
* The Shaykh: The hand masculine?!
* The Student: (...).
* The Shaykh: Yes, (...) ﴿Insert your hand into your bosom; it will come out white﴾ [al-Qasas 32]; he did not say "it will come out white (abyad)." And Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Rather, both His hands are outstretched﴾ [al-Ma'idah 64], and He said: ﴿The Jews say: the hand of Allah is fettered﴾ [al-Ma'idah 64], and others. The point is that it is feminine.
So the staff is feminine and the hand is feminine.
Now, the demonstrative ﴿fadhanika burhanan﴾ [al-Qasas 32], is it masculine or not? From the demonstrative, and if it were feminine he would have said: "tanika burhanan." So why did he make it masculine?
The author says: (and the demonstrative referring to them was made masculine to agree with its predicate), because ("dhan") is the subject, and the predicate is ﴿two proofs﴾: (to agree with the masculine of its predicate, ﴿two proofs﴾).
﴿Burhanan﴾ is the dual of burhan, and burhan is masculine or feminine?
* Student: Masculine.
* The Shaykh: Masculine?
* The Student: Yes indeed.
* The Shaykh: (...) ﴿O mankind, there has come to you a proof (burhan) from your Lord﴾ [al-Nisa' 174]; though this is not clearly evident to us, since the verb and its subject are separated. He did not say "there have come to you a proof." ﴿There has come to you a burhan﴾.
So burhan is masculine, and the hand and the staff are feminine. Here the predicate was taken into account, not the thing pointed to. The predicate was taken into account, because ﴿burhanan﴾ is masculine, so the demonstrative was made masculine.
﴿Burhanan﴾: what is the burhan? It is the proof.
As for the author's words, (two messengers (mursalan) ﴿from your Lord﴾), the word (mursalan) is not an explanation of ﴿burhanan﴾, but a clarification of what the prepositional phrase depends on. His words ﴿from your Lord﴾ depend on it, because the word burhan is a rigid noun, and a prepositional phrase cannot depend on a rigid noun. Have you understood, O people, or not?
Again we say: (mursalan) might be thought by someone to be an explanation of burhan, but burhan does not mean "sent"; burhan means proof. A clear proof is called a burhan, and the theologians say: burhan is a decisive, conclusive proof.
But the author inserted (mursalan) to show that his words ﴿from your Lord﴾ depend on the implied (mursalan), and did not make it depend on ﴿burhanan﴾, because ﴿burhanan﴾ is a rigid noun, and a prepositional phrase depends only on a verb or a derivative noun, as the versifier said:
"A prepositional phrase must depend on a verb or on something of its meaning, like 'murtaqi' (ascending)."
"And exclude every extra particle that has governance, like ba', min, ka', and also la'alla."
The evidence is his words: "a prepositional phrase must depend on a verb or what carries its meaning," meaning: (mursalan).
But other than the author said: there is no need to supply (mursalan); rather we say: ﴿burhanan﴾ are existing from your Lord, so it depends (...) like other prepositional phrases. But what those who differed with him said is more correct than what the author said, because what the author said is specific, and what others estimated is general, and when the dependent of a prepositional phrase is specific it is not permissible to omit it; it must be mentioned. So the dependent of a prepositional phrase is not omitted unless it is general, such as "existing" (ka'in), "present" (mawjud), or the like.
So the correct view is to leave the verse as it is, and say: ﴿from your Lord﴾ depends on an omitted element whose estimate is: (existing).
﴿Two proofs from your Lord to Pharaoh and his chiefs﴾ [al-Qasas 32]. This is what led the author to estimate (mursalan), for the sake of his words ﴿to Pharaoh﴾; but he is not the sender. The sender in reality is who? Musa. But with him are two proofs ﴿to Pharaoh and his chiefs﴾, that is his people. Pharaoh is the ruler of Egypt, and it has been said that he is a generic proper name for every disbelieving ruler of Egypt; every disbelieving ruler of Egypt is called Pharaoh, and every disbelieving ruler of Persia is called Chosroes (Kisra), and every disbelieving ruler of Rome is called Caesar (Qaysar).
His words ﴿Indeed they were a corrupt people﴾ [al-Qasas 32]: the sentence is a reason for what precedes it, meaning: We sent you with these two signs to these people because they were a corrupt people.
﴿They were﴾ in the past, or ﴿they were﴾ in Allah's knowledge?
* Student: (...).
* The Shaykh: We established earlier that (kana) is detached from time, detached in indicating time; that is, it does not indicate past or otherwise. So the meaning of ﴿they were a corrupt people﴾ is: characterized by corruption. We established this because (kana) does not indicate the negation of past time. We established this because Allah the Exalted says of Himself always: ﴿And Allah has ever been Knowing of all things﴾ [al-Ahzab 40], ﴿And Allah has ever been Forgiving and Merciful﴾ [al-Nisa' 96], and so on to the end. It is known that the intended meaning is not past time, but that He is characterized by these attributes; yet it may indicate past time through a context other than the wording of the verb.
As for his words ﴿corrupt (fasiqin)﴾, which of the two kinds of corruption is meant? Disbelieving corruption or obedient corruption?
(...). It has passed for us that corruption divides into two kinds: one that takes one out of the religion, which is the corruption of disbelief, and a corruption that takes one out of uprightness, which is the corruption of sin, sin without disbelief. An example of the first?
* Student: (...).
* The Shaykh: An example other than this verse?
* Student: (...).
* The Shaykh: Yes, possible, but there are clearer verses than it; it contains detail (...).
* Student: (...).
* The Shaykh: No. ﴿Is one who was a believer like one who was a corrupt? They are not equal. As for those who believed and did righteous deeds, for them are gardens of refuge as hospitality for what they used to do. But as for those who defiantly disobeyed, their refuge is the Fire﴾ [al-Sajdah 18-20].
An example of corruption that does not take one out of faith: ﴿O you who have believed, if a corrupt person brings you a report, verify it, lest you harm a people out of ignorance﴾ [al-Hujurat 6].
* Student: (...)?
* The Shaykh: The chiefs? The chiefs (...), and it appears, and Allah knows best, that just as (...).
Second: the wisdom of Allah the Exalted as well, in that He gives the prophets signs suited to the time and the condition of those to whom they are sent, because this is wisdom, that the signs should match the reality.
* Among its lessons also: this sign given to Musa, namely that when he draws his hand in and brings it out, it comes out white without any defect.
* Among them: Allah the Blessed and Exalted guiding Musa, when he fears something, to draw his hand to himself until he is reassured and his heart is calm. Is this specific to him or general? It was previously mentioned that it was narrated from Ibn 'Abbas that if one fears something, he should place his hand on his chest.[[Abu Muhammad al-Qayrawani mentioned in his tafsir al-Hidayah ila Bulugh al-Nihayah (8/5530) from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: No one is seized by terror after Musa, then inserts his hand and draws it to his chest, except that the terror departs from him.]] So it would be general. The apparent view is that it is specific to Musa, because a person may use this and it does not benefit him at all.
* Among them: the confirmation and support of the prophets with signs that indicate their truthfulness; from His words ﴿These two are proofs﴾ [al-Qasas 32].
* Among them: that the signs that come to the prophets are proofs against their peoples, because burhan means proof and argument, so the signs that give them are proofs against their peoples, that they are obligated to apply them, is that right?

**Ibn 'Uthaymin's Commentary (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on Surah 28, Verse 32 (Part 2 of 2)**

* Among its benefits: no messenger is sent except that he is given a sign (āyah) that shows his truthfulness. For if he were not given a sign, people would have an excuse for rejecting him (...). Do you know why? Because if he came and said, "I am the Messenger of the Lord of the worlds, and you must do such-and-such and avoid such-and-such," they might say, "We cannot act except with clear proof (bayyinah)," and the bayyinah is the signs (āyāt).
* Among its benefits: the kindness (luṭf) of Allah, may He be blessed and exalted, toward His servants, in that He sends messengers to them for their own benefit and not for His benefit. Allah says: ﴿And whoever disbelieves, then indeed Allah is Free of need from the worlds﴾ [Āl ʿImrān 3:97]. Rather, for the benefit of creation He sends messengers to them.
* Among the benefits of the verse: a messenger is sent wherever people need one to bring them out of disobedience to Allah. This is based on His saying: ﴿Indeed, they were a defiant people﴾ [al-Qaṣaṣ 28:32].
* Among its benefits: Allah, glorified and exalted, renews this ummah's religion whenever it departs from it. From where do we take this?
* Student: (...).

So instead of a messenger, there is raised from among them a knowledgeable, teaching man who goes out to them, whether he is a ruler from the rulers of authority or (...). The important thing is that one knows that Allah, glorified and exalted, sends messengers when people are in need of them, and in this ummah there is no messenger, so there remain (...) righteous, reforming people raised up from among its folk, who reform creation.
* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: Yes, (...).
Also among its benefits: it is generally the case that the followers of the leaders of disbelief are the nobles. This is based on His saying: ﴿to Pharaoh and his chiefs﴾ [al-Qaṣaṣ 28:32]. For al-mala' (the chiefs, the notables) are the nobles, although the term is also applied to the people in general. Allah mentions in another verse: ﴿to Pharaoh and his people, indeed they were a defiant people﴾ [al-Naml 27:12]. But generally al-mala' are the nobles, and they are the ones who usually come to be arrogant toward what the messengers brought, while the weak and the poor follow them.
* Student: (...)?
* Shaykh: Yes, yes.
* Student: (...)?
* Shaykh: This is the apparent meaning, but perhaps, and Allah knows best, (...), at the head of every hundred (years) [Abū Dāwūd (4291) narrated with his chain from Abū Hurayrah, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who said: "Indeed Allah sends to this ummah, at the head of every hundred years, someone who renews its religion for it."] So this may be the upper limit, (...).
He says: ﴿And my brother Hārūn﴾.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 28, verse 33–36 (part 1 of 3):

He said: ﴿And my brother Harun, he is more eloquent in tongue than me, so send him with me as a helper, to confirm me﴾ [al-Qasas 34].

First: What is the grammatical analysis (i'rab) of this sentence, ﴿And my brother Harun, he is more eloquent in tongue than me﴾?

﴿akhi (my brother)﴾ is a subject (mubtada'), or not? "Akhi" is the subject (mubtada').

The essential point is his saying: ﴿he is more eloquent in tongue than me﴾ [al-Qasas 34]. Then we ask: is ﴿huwa﴾ a pronoun of separation (damir al-fasl), or is ﴿huwa﴾ the subject (mubtada') and ﴿afsahu (more eloquent)﴾ the predicate (khabar), with the sentence serving as the predicate of the subject (...)? Because the pronoun of separation (...), and the subject and predicate are both definite (ma'rifatan); because in this case the predicate could be confused with a verb. But if the predicate is indefinite (nakirah), as here, then it is treated as the subject.

He said: ﴿And my brother Harun﴾ [al-Qasas 34]. Is he his brother from both mother and father, or from the father alone?

From both his mother and his father. As for the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿O son of my mother, do not seize me by my beard nor by my head﴾ [Ta-Ha 94], they mentioned that his attribution to his mother is because she is closer than the father, so he mentioned her (...) to make him feel compassion.

He said: ﴿And my brother Harun, he is more eloquent in tongue than me﴾ [al-Qasas 34].

﴿Afsah (more eloquent)﴾ means more clear (abyan) than me. His saying ﴿lisanan (in tongue)﴾ means speech (kalaman), and he expressed speech by "tongue" because it is the instrument of speech. Allah the Blessed and Exalted said: ﴿And We did not send any messenger except with the tongue of his people﴾ [Ibrahim 4], meaning with their speech and their language.

As for his saying ﴿more eloquent than me in tongue﴾, why? It has been said in the Isra'iliyyat (narrations from Israelite sources) that Musa, peace be upon him, had in his tongue (...) from a live coal he took and ate, when Pharaoh wanted to kill him, and his wife said: "He is a child who does not understand or know. If you want to test him, give him a date and a coal." So she presented to him the date and the coal; the coal was glittering and its appearance more beautiful than the date, so he took the coal and put it in his mouth, and his tongue became tied. This is an Isra'iliyyah, because this is not possible; for if he wanted to take the coal and took it, he could not hold it in his hand (...). For this reason Musa asked Allah to untie this knot, saying: ﴿And untie a knot from my tongue (27), that they may understand my speech﴾ [Ta-Ha 27, 28].

And you see some people who have a stammer in their tongue (fafa'ah), and some who have a lisp (ta'ta'ah) (...), and some who have neither this nor that, but cannot speak; you find that when he wants to speak—may Allah protect us—his face turns red and he gets tired (...). So the knot (ʿuqdah) is the same whether in the manner of the letters or in pronouncing the letter. Both are types of knots. In the manner of the letters: he cannot bring them out in their most complete form; or in the very act of pronunciation: he cannot, his tongue does not move freely.

So the correct view is that this defect in Musa, peace be upon him, was from the origin of his creation, and there was no date and coal.

He said: (﴿So send him with me as a helper﴾ [al-Qasas 34], a supporter (mu'in), and in one reading with a fathah on the dal without a hamzah), how do we say it? ﴿radan (a supporter)﴾, meaning (...) ﴿so send him with me as a helper (ridan)﴾.

Musa, peace be upon him, understood that Allah had sent him to Pharaoh from His saying: ﴿These two are proofs from your Lord to Pharaoh﴾ [al-Qasas 32]. For this reason he said: ﴿so send him with me﴾, and so here he knew that he was a messenger.

As for his saying ﴿ma'iya (with me)﴾, the "mi'iyyah" means companionship and accompaniment, and it is in each place according to what it is attached to, meaning according to what it is added to, and in each place it implies something different from what it implies in another place. So when it is said "the man is with his wife," it is not like when it is said "the commander is with his soldiers," or not? So there is a difference between them. Likewise when it is said "the milk is with the water," meaning mixed and blended with it. Here, ﴿so send him with me as a helper﴾ is not the companionship of a husband with his wife nor the companionship of milk with water; rather, it is an accompaniment intended for support and victory, and for this he said: ﴿ridan (a helper)﴾, and the ridf is the one who aids and backs a person.

﴿Yusaddiqunee (to confirm me)﴾: what is the meaning of ﴿yusaddiqunee﴾? It means that he would be one who confirms me before them, so that my words are strengthened by him and become true; and the meaning is not that he says, "You are truthful." Rather, when his speech strengthens my speech, that becomes a cause for their believing him.

He said: (In the jussive (bil-jazm) as the answer to the supplication; and in one reading in the nominative (bil-raf'), and its clause is a description (sifah) of ﴿ridan﴾).

(In the jussive): you say ﴿yusaddiqni﴾ is the answer to the supplication. Where is the supplication? ﴿so send him with me﴾, and this is clear, meaning: if you send him, he will confirm me.

(And in another reading): is this a Sab'i (canonical seven) reading or a shadhdh (irregular) one? Sab'i, because the author's rule, may Allah have mercy on him, is that when he says "in a reading" (fi qira'ah) it is Sab'i, and when he says "it was read" (wa-quri'a) it is shadhdh.

He said: ﴿So send him with me as a helper, to confirm me﴾, and its clause in the nominative reading is a description of ﴿ridan﴾, meaning: a helper confirming me. This is the detail.

* A student: (...)?
* The Shaykh: Yes, good. The benefit of the two readings (...) is a benefit, which is that his saying ﴿yusaddiqunee﴾, if it is the answer (to the request), then its meaning is that truthfulness is achieved through him; and if it is a description, then the meaning is that he tries to (...) or tries to show the people that he is truthful. So the nominative reading is by way of cause, and the jussive reading by way of result, so Harun is an active, influential agent.

He said: ﴿Indeed I fear that they will deny me﴾ [al-Qasas 34]. The pronoun in ﴿yukadhdhibun (they deny)﴾ is the plural waw pronoun referring to Pharaoh and his chiefs.

﴿Akhafu (I fear)﴾ means I expect and I dread, and it is not the fear of terror; there is no terror here, but he anticipates that and dreads it.

As for his saying ﴿an yukadhdhibun (that they deny)﴾, there is a difficulty in terms of grammar, because it is known that when ﴿an﴾ enters upon the five verbs (al-af'al al-khamsah), the nun is removed from them, and here there is a nun?

The answer: this nun is the nun of protection (nun al-waqayah), not the nun of inflection (nun al-i'rab), and for this you see it now with a kasrah. So the original is ("an yukadhdhibunanee") — the original is "yukadhdhibunanee," so the nun of the nominative was removed because of the accusative, and the ya was removed for lightness.

A parallel to it is His saying, the Exalted, in the same type in Surat al-Dhariyat: ﴿Indeed for those who did wrong is a portion like the portion of their companions, so let them not seek to hasten (fa-la yasta'jilun)﴾ [al-Dhariyat 59]. If you stop on it, you stop with sukun, so the beginner student who has no knowledge of grammar understands that here the nun remains with the presence of the prohibitive "la," and with the prohibitive "la" it must be removed. But we say: this nun in the verse is the nun of protection, as evidence that if you join it, you would make it kasrah and say: ﴿fa-la yasta'jilunee (59) fa-waylun﴾ [al-Dhariyat 59, 60]. Yes, is that so?

* A student: Yes.
* The Shaykh: Good. The author said, yes, Allah the Exalted said: (﴿We will strengthen your arm﴾ [al-Qasas 35], we will empower you).

Shadd (strengthening) means empowering, and the 'adud is the complete bone between the forearm and the shoulder; this is the 'adud, and strengthening the arm is a metaphor for empowerment, since the hand is the instrument of action; when its arm is strengthened and made firm, it becomes strong. The meaning is that We will empower you and support you with your brother ﴿We will strengthen your arm with your brother﴾ [al-Qasas 35], Harun. Did Allah answer his request or not? Allah answered his request, and said: ﴿We will strengthen﴾, and the sin (sin), what does it mean?

* A student: It indicates postponement (taswif).

* The Shaykh: Yes, it indicates postponement, but what do the grammarians say about its grammatical function?

* The student: (...).

* The Shaykh: For expansion (tanfis), which is for postponement; "sawfa" is for expansion, and it indicates strengthening of emphasis and proximity, the emphasis of a thing and bringing it near, that it will happen soon.

He said: ﴿We will strengthen your arm with your brother﴾. There is no doubt that when Allah says this to him, it means that he is being strengthened now, because Allah's promise is not merely to send Harun with him, but that he will be a helper to him in this matter.

(﴿And We will give you both authority﴾ [al-Qasas 35], domination), and this is a second glad tiding to both of them.

﴿And We will make﴾ is the counterpart of "for you both authority (sultanan)." The meaning of "sultan" here, the author says, is "domination (ghalabah)," and "sultan" in the Qur'an comes with the meaning of domination and power, and comes with the meaning of proof, because a person is strengthened by proof and has authority through it. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿You have no authority for this; do you say about Allah what you do not know?﴾ [Yunus 68]. What does ﴿you have no authority for this﴾ mean? It means: you have no proof for this. And His saying the Exalted: ﴿So pass through; you will not pass except with authority﴾ [al-Rahman 33], meaning with strength and domination. And His saying: ﴿His authority is only over those who take him as an ally﴾ [al-Nahl 100], meaning his control and domination.

Here he says: ﴿And We will give you both authority﴾ [al-Qasas 35], and says: (domination), so it is from the second category.

(﴿So they will not reach you both﴾ [al-Qasas 35] with harm): the meaning is that they will not reach you both with harm; so what you feared from them will be removed by what Allah has made for you of support through your brother. This is a glad tiding to both of them and serves to strengthen them, and it is similar to His saying the Exalted: ﴿Do not fear; indeed I am with you both, hearing and seeing﴾ [Ta-Ha 46].

The author said: (Go ﴿with Our signs﴾), it seems that the author sees that His saying ﴿with Our signs﴾ is separate from His saying ﴿And We will give you both authority﴾, and for this he estimated a verb for it to be attached to, and on this estimation the pause would be at His saying ﴿So they will not reach you both﴾, and we begin and say: ﴿with Our signs, you two and whoever follows you, are the victorious﴾ [al-Qasas 35].

Good, the author estimated (Go ﴿with Our signs﴾), then he also said (...) ﴿you two and whoever follows you are the victorious﴾, so the verse becomes, according to the author's estimation: ﴿And We will make for you both authority, so they will not reach you both﴾, ﴿with Our signs﴾, ﴿you two and whoever follows you are the victorious﴾; because he estimated (Go ﴿with Our signs﴾), and it is not appropriate to say ﴿you two and whoever follows you are the victorious﴾ as a continuation of it, because whoever followed them did not go with the signs. Do you understand, everyone?

* A student: Yes.

* The Shaykh: Good, this is one view.

Another view they say: His saying ﴿with Our signs﴾ is attached to ﴿And We will make﴾: "And We will make for you both authority with Our signs," meaning: because of Our signs We will make for you both authority, so they cannot reach you both nor nullify your call. On this, is there a need for an estimate in the verse or not?

* A student: No need.

* The Shaykh: No need for an estimate. And should we stop at His saying ﴿so they will not reach you both﴾ or continue? We continue, so the reading is: ﴿so they will not reach you both with Our signs﴾ [al-Qasas 35], meaning: because of the signs that you have. This meaning is the correct one. First: because it does not need an estimate, since an estimate, everyone, must be preceded by two stages: the first stage: establishing that there is an omission (hadhf) in the speech; the second stage: establishing that the estimated omitted element is this one, or not? (...) or another. The claim must be preceded by two stages: the first stage is establishing that there is an omission in the speech requiring explanation, and the second is establishing that the estimated element is this, meaning specifying the estimate; because even if we grant that the verse needs an estimate, it may be disputed, and it may be said to him: what is this estimate you have estimated? We do not grant that the estimate of the omitted element is this (...). Everyone who claims an omission in a verse needs two things or two stages: the first stage: establishing that there is an omission in the speech, and by what way do we know this? If the speech does not stand without an estimate, we know that there is an omission; this is one.

The second stage: establishing that the omitted element is this thing you estimated, since it is permissible that the estimate is something else, or not? And this is certainly an estimate determined by the context, because the context is what specifies the type of the omitted element.

Good, if the speech does not need this estimate, then it is better not to estimate. The meaning of this verse is very clear on the view of no estimate, and that the meaning is: We will make for you both authority by means of Our signs that are with you, so they will not reach you both; and this meaning is also clearer than what the author and others estimated, because in reality he says: ﴿with Our signs﴾ here is plural, and in the first he says: ﴿These two are proofs from your Lord to Pharaoh and his chiefs﴾ [al-Qasas 32]. So did Allah send them, when He sent them, with only one sign or with two signs? Two signs.

The correct view, then, is that the verse is connected, its parts joined to one another, and we read: ﴿so they will not reach you both with Our signs﴾, yes: ﴿And We will make for you both authority, so they will not reach you both with Our signs﴾, and it is attached to His saying: "We will make for you both authority with Our signs, so they will not reach you both."

Some of the grammarians claimed that His saying ﴿with Our signs﴾ is attached to ﴿the victorious﴾, and this in meaning is close to what we mentioned, meaning: "You two and whoever follows you are the victorious with Our signs." The one victorious by the signs is the one to whom authority was given through them, so on this view: "so they will not reach you both; you two and whoever follows you are the victorious with Our signs." Without doubt this is better than the author's estimate, because it needs no omission, and because it makes the speech connected in part to part; but there is an omission from the standpoint of grammatical rules, which is that ﴿the victorious﴾ is an active participle (ism fa'il), and the "al" attached to the active participle is, according to the grammarians, what? A relative pronoun:

"And a clear adjective, the ṣilah of (al) ..."

A relative pronoun, and it is known that a relative pronoun's complement does not operate on what precedes it; its complement does not govern, so we then need an answer to this rule.

The answer they gave: the "al" here is not relative, but like the "al" that enters on a fixed noun, entering on "the man" and "the lion" and similar.

So in this estimate there is a violation of the known grammatical rules.

We return now to the view that the correct approach is to make His saying ﴿with Our signs﴾ attached to ﴿And We will make for you both authority﴾, and we are spared all that: the violations, the estimates we rely on, and the specification of the estimated element.

And His saying ﴿with Our signs﴾, ﴿so they will not reach you both with Our signs﴾, contains evidence that Allah the Exalted gave Musa and Harun signs; and He mentioned in another surah that He gave him nine signs, or not? ﴿And We certainly gave Musa nine clear signs, so ask the Children of Israel when he came to them﴾ [al-Isra' 101].

And His saying ﴿you two and whoever follows you﴾: who are they? From the Children of Israel and from the family of Pharaoh, because among the family of Pharaoh were those who followed them, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And a believing man from the family of Pharaoh said﴾ [Ghafir 28].

And His saying ﴿and whoever follows you﴾ contains evidence that a person is aided and made victorious by following the messengers, and that there is no path to victory and dominance except entering the path of the messengers and following them. Accordingly, there is from this a rule: whoever is more closely following the Messenger is nearer to victory, and whoever is further from following the Messenger is further from victory; because it is known among the established rules that when a ruling is attached to an attribute, its establishment is in strength and weakness, existence and non-existence, according to that attribute. When a ruling is attached to an attribute, the establishment of the ruling is in existence and non-existence, strength and weakness, according to that attribute, understood?

For example: ﴿Indeed Allah is with the patient﴾ [al-Baqarah 153]: His companionship with the patient is in strength and weakness according to the patience they have.

﴿Indeed Allah is with those who are mindful of Him﴾ [al-Nahl 128]: the existence of companionship for the God-conscious is in strength and weakness according to their God-consciousness... and so on.

The Shaykh (Ibn 'Uthaymin) said, in his commentary on Allah's words:

﴿أَنْتُمَا وَمَنِ اتَّبَعَكُمَا الْغَالِبُونَ﴾ [al-Qasas 28:35] "You two and those who follow you will be the victors." **Al-ghalibun** (the victors): over whom? The author says: "(the victors) over them." ... But if we want to take this in its general sense, we say: ﴿أَنْتُمَا وَمَنِ اتَّبَعَكُمَا الْغَالِبُونَ﴾ means victorious over those who oppose them. The followers of the messengers are victorious over those who oppose the messengers, always and forever, or not? Always and forever. Indeed, these matters (...) over others. The Prophet ﷺ said: "I have been helped with terror (of my enemy) for a distance of one month."[[Agreed upon (Muttafaqun 'alayh). Al-Bukhari (438) and Muslim (521/3), from the hadith of Jabir ibn 'Abdullah, may Allah be pleased with him and his father.]] Allahu akbar! How great this benefit is, if only we were at the level we should be! If we truly followed this noble Prophet ﷺ in reality, our enemy would be terrified of us for a distance of one month. But, unfortunately, we were not truly following the Messenger, peace be upon him, in reality.
