Therefore our might has become between ourselves, neither those who claim Islam among us, nor those who wish to shelter under the principle of jahiliyyah, which is Arab nationalism (al-qawmiyyah al-'arabiyyah). Nationalism has not triumphed since its emergence until today, and it will never triumph. Rather, it only increases in failure, division and fragmentation, and indeed, fighting among its own. Likewise, in reality, we have not united on an Islamic nationality; we have not united on it. So the Muslims remain neither on this nor on that, and therefore we did not have the victory which Allah promised to His Prophet ﷺ.

He said: (﴿فَلَمَّا جَاءَهُمْ مُوسَى بِآيَاتِنَا بَيِّنَاتٍ﴾ [al-Qasas 28:36] clear, as a circumstantial state (hal)).

﴿فَلَمَّا جَاءَهُمْ﴾ means: the people of Pharaoh (Ali Fir'awn).

﴿مُوسَى بِآيَاتِنَا﴾: He did not say "and Harun," because the messengership originally belonged to Musa.

As for ﴿بِآيَاتِنَا﴾, the letter ba' indicates accompaniment, meaning accompanied by the signs.

﴿بِآيَاتِنَا﴾ is the plural of ayah, which means signs. It is attributed to Allah as the attribution of a gift to its giver, because these signs are not signs upon Allah; rather they are signs from Him, upon what? Upon the messengership of Musa, and Musa, within it, is proof that Allah alone is the true God.

﴿بِآيَاتِنَا بَيِّنَاتٍ﴾: He said "clear," and regarding its i'rab (grammatical analysis) he said: "a circumstantial state (hal)." A hal of what? (...)

Student: Of (ayat).

Shaykh: Of (ayat). And it is not correct to be an adjective (sifah)?

Student: (...)

Shaykh: Is it correct or not correct? Give me the ruling before the reason.

Student: It is not correct.

Shaykh: It is not correct, because (ayat) is definite (ma'rifah), and ﴿بَيِّنَاتٍ﴾ is indefinite (nakirah), and a definite noun is not described by an indefinite noun. Rather, when an indefinite noun comes after a definite noun and is its description, it is parsed as a hal.

In His words ﴿بِآيَاتِنَا بَيِّنَاتٍ﴾ there is an establishment of proof, because an ayah is a sign, and whenever it is more evident, the proof is stronger. So the signs are clear.

He brought them the clear signs, so what answer came from them?

(﴿قَالُوا مَا هَذَا إِلَّا سِحْرٌ مُفْتَرًى﴾ [al-Qasas 28:36] fabricated (mukhtalaq)). I seek refuge in Allah.

﴿مَا هَذَا﴾ means: what you have brought, O Musa, ﴿إِلَّا سِحْرٌ﴾. Here we ask: why did "ma" not act like "laysa," although the dialect of the Hijaz makes it act like "laysa"? Because Ibn Malik says?

Student: (...)

Shaykh: Yes. Its meaning is that the negation must remain, and here the negation did not remain, so it was nullified by (...)

Their saying ﴿مَا هَذَا إِلَّا سِحْرٌ مُفْتَرًى﴾: what is the magic they meant (...)?

Student: The staff.

Shaykh: The staff and the hand. This is if we say that it refers to the sensory signs. But if we say that it refers to the non-sensory signs, which are like speech, then the Prophet, peace be upon him, said: "Indeed, some eloquence is magic."[[Narrated by al-Bukhari (5767), from the hadith of 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with him and his father.]]

As for His words (﴿مُفْتَرًى﴾ fabricated (mukhtalaq)): the attribution of fabrication to the speech is clear, but the attribution of fabrication to the staff and the hand? Because magic does not truly change things; it changes them only in imagination, according to what a person imagines. So is this imagining in agreement with reality or contrary to reality? And everything that contradicts reality is fabricated; everything that contradicts reality is fabricated. Take care, O people.

So, the fabrication here, if it is attributed to what they said of the message, is problematic.

Student: (...)

Shaykh: Clear. If it is attributed to what they said of the message, is it problematic or clear? It is clear, because attributing fabrication to speech is a known matter. But if it is attributed to what he brought of sensory signs, such as the transformation of the staff and the hand emerging white, then how can we say it is fabricated? Because magic does not turn a matter from its reality; it does not change it from its reality. So its appearance in a state other than its true one is a kind of lying and calumny. Therefore they said: ﴿إِلَّا سِحْرٌ مُفْتَرًى﴾.

(﴿وَمَا سَمِعْنَا بِهَذَا﴾ present (ka'innan) ﴿فِي﴾ the days of ﴿آبَائِنَا الْأَوَّلِينَ﴾ [al-Qasas 28:36]) (...)

﴿وَمَا سَمِعْنَا بِهَذَا فِي آبَائِنَا الْأَوَّلِينَ﴾.

﴿وَمَا سَمِعْنَا بِهَذَا﴾: the referent of "this" is what he brought of the message, because it is what is heard; as for the sign of the hand and the staff, it is witnessed and seen.

As for His words ﴿فِي آبَائِنَا﴾, the commentator, the author, said: "present (ka'innan)," indicating that the complement of the prepositional phrase with ﴿آبَائِنَا الْأَوَّلِينَ﴾ is omitted, its estimate being "present."

Is "present (ka'innan)" here, according to the author's estimate, a second object or a circumstantial state?

A circumstantial state of the demonstrative.

As for His words ﴿فِي آبَائِنَا الْأَوَّلِينَ﴾, it means: in their time, and therefore he said: "in the days of our first forefathers," meaning the earlier ones.

Is their statement true or false?

Student: False.

Shaykh: And why would they lie?

Student: (...) ﴿وَلَقَدْ جَاءَكُمْ يُوسُفُ مِنْ قَبْلُ﴾.

Shaykh: Yes: ﴿بِالْبَيِّنَاتِ فَمَا زِلْتُمْ فِي شَكٍّ مِمَّا جَاءَكُمْ بِهِ حَتَّى إِذَا هَلَكَ قُلْتُمْ لَنْ يَبْعَثَ اللَّهُ مِنْ بَعْدِهِ رَسُولًا﴾ [Ghafir 40:34] "with clear proofs; but you remained in doubt about what he brought you, until, when he died, you said: 'Allah will never send after him a messenger.'"

So their saying ﴿وَمَا سَمِعْنَا بِهَذَا فِي آبَائِنَا الْأَوَّلِينَ﴾ [al-Qasas 28:36] is a false report, and they are liars in this claim. Then, supposing the claim is true and they had not heard of it, does the fact that this did not exist among the earlier ones necessitate that it is false for the later ones?

Student: It does not necessitate it.

Shaykh: It does not necessitate it, because when the truth comes, it must be accepted, whether or not it existed among the earlier ones. So this argument is composed of falsehood and nonsense: as for the falsehood, their saying ﴿وَمَا سَمِعْنَا بِهَذَا فِي آبَائِنَا الْأَوَّلِينَ﴾ is a lie, because their believer had established proof against them by the existence of a parallel to what Musa brought, in His words: ﴿وَلَقَدْ جَاءَكُمْ يُوسُفُ مِنْ قَبْلُ بِالْبَيِّنَاتِ﴾. As for it being a false argument on the assumption that it is true in its statement, it is because the absence of that among the earlier ones does not necessitate the falsity of its existence among the later ones, for Allah, the Exalted, does what He wills. So as long as the signs are clear, there is no proof in that they did not occur before.

As for His words ﴿فِي آبَائِنَا الْأَوَّلِينَ﴾: how can he say ﴿الْأَوَّلِينَ﴾ when they are fathers?

Because "father" (ab) is applied to the direct father and to the grandfather, however far up. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿مِلَّةَ أَبِيكُمْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ هُوَ سَمَّاكُمُ﴾ [al-Hajj 22:78] "the religion of your father Ibrahim; He named you..." And Yusuf said: ﴿وَاتَّبَعْتُ مِلَّةَ آبَائِي إِبْرَاهِيمَ وَإِسْحَاقَ وَيَعْقُوبَ﴾ [Yusuf 12:38] "And I followed the religion of my forefathers, Ibrahim, Ishaq and Ya'qub." Ya'qub was his direct father, Ishaq was his grandfather, and Ibrahim was his grandfather's father. He called them fathers. Although this involves the principle of prominence (taghlib), in ﴿مِلَّةَ أَبِيكُمْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ﴾ there is no prominence, meaning there is no direct father in it. Therefore the preferred view regarding (...) is that the grandfather...

Student: He blocks the grandfather.

Shaykh: He blocks the grandfather, and that Allah...

Student: (...)?

Shaykh: This is specific to the apparent sense. But ﴿ومَا سَمِعْنَا بِهَذَا﴾ [al-Qasas 28:36] (...)

* * *

From this is derived: the permissibility of offering an excuse when commanded to do something, in order to be released from (...). Yes, even in obeying the ruler, for example: if he commands you to do something, obedience to him is obligatory in what is not sinful, and there is no harm in mentioning an excuse in order to be exempted from this command, just as the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, used to present excuses to the Prophet ﷺ when he commanded them to do something, so that he would excuse them.

* And it is derived from it that natural fear does not contradict the station of messengership, by His words: ﴿فَأَخَافُ أَنْ يَقْتُلُونِ﴾ [al-Qasas 28:33] "I fear that they will kill me."

* And it is derived from it that retaliation (qisas) existed in earlier times (...), existing among the previous nations; by His words: ﴿فَأَخَافُ أَنْ يَقْتُلُونِ﴾, meaning in exchange for his killing (...). So do we say that this was by way of retaliation, or by way of aggression from the family of Pharaoh? That is, they may not have cared. If we applied this to the Islamic ruling it would be deficient, because a Muslim is not killed for a disbeliever. So we say: this, His words ﴿فَأَخَافُ أَنْ يَقْتُلُونِ﴾, is either because retaliation was well known among them, or because he feared they would attack him with killing, even if that was not by right. And as long as it is a possibility, it cannot be taken as evidence for (...).

* * *

﴿وَأَخِي هَارُونُ هُوَ أَفْصَحُ مِنِّي لِسَانًا﴾, what?

Student: (...)?

Shaykh: Same, (...).

He said: ﴿وَأَخِي هَارُونُ هُوَ أَفْصَحُ مِنِّي لِسَانًا فَأَرْسِلْهُ مَعِيَ رِدْءًا يُصَدِّقُنِي إِنِّي أَخَافُ أَنْ يُكَذِّبُونِ﴾ [al-Qasas 28:34] "And my brother Harun is more eloquent in tongue than I, so send him with me as a helper to confirm me; indeed, I fear that they will deny me."

* From this is derived: the great favour of Musa toward his brother, in that Allah the Exalted made it so that He sent him with him. Therefore it is said: the greatest gift a beloved gave to his beloved is that which Musa gave to Harun, because he asked Allah to send him with him, and messengership is a great station which none attains except the choicest of the sons of Adam.

Student: (...).

Shaykh: * And also among the benefits, from the benefits of the verse: it is permissible for a person to seek help from others in calling to Allah, the Exalted; by His words: ﴿فَأَرْسِلْهُ مَعِيَ رِدْءًا﴾ [al-Qasas 28:34].

* And also: that taking helpers is one of the causes of success, and this is a known matter from ancient times and modern, that whenever a person has someone with him who helps and supports him, that is closer to his success than being alone. The common people say: "one hand does not clap."

* And among them: eloquence has an effect; eloquence of tongue has a strong effect on acceptance or rejection. The Prophet ﷺ said: "Indeed, some eloquence is magic,"[[Narrated by al-Bukhari (5767), from the hadith of 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar.]] by His words: ﴿هُوَ أَفْصَحُ مِنِّي لِسَانًا﴾.

* And among them: the virtue of Musa, peace be upon him, by his acknowledgment of his brother's superiority: ﴿هُوَ أَفْصَحُ مِنِّي لِسَانًا﴾, because some people are deficient but cannot express the perfection of others while acknowledging their own deficiency.

* And among its benefits: that the caller should mention the justifications for his call, because his saying ﴿هُوَ أَفْصَحُ مِنِّي لِسَانًا فَأَرْسِلْهُ﴾ [al-Qasas 28:34] is one of the justifications for his call and his request that Allah, blessed and exalted, send him with him, namely that he is more eloquent in tongue. This is known (...) among the etiquette of callers, that a person mentions the justifications of the call, saying: "By Allah (...)."

* And also, from the noble verses: Musa, peace be upon him, feared that they would deny him if he were alone, so he sought further help, because, as we said, one with another is closer to being believed.

* And also from it: that a report becomes more firmly established by the multiplicity of its reporters, or not?

Student: (...).

Shaykh: Yes.

Student: He said (...).

Shaykh: Yes, not (...).

Student: (...)?

Shaykh: (...) helps him; because the essence of messengership is a report, so if he has with him someone who strengthens this report, confirms it and validates it, it becomes stronger. And the establishment of a report by the multiplicity of its reporters is also a known matter, but (...).

* * *

﴿قَالَ سَنَشُدُّ عَضُدَكَ بِأَخِيكَ وَنَجْعَلُ لَكُمَا سُلْطَانًا فَلَا يَصِلُونَ إِلَيْكُمَا بِآيَاتِنَا أَنْتُمَا وَمَنِ اتَّبَعَكُمَا الْغَالِبُونَ﴾ [al-Qasas 28:35] "He said: We will strengthen your arm through your brother, and We will give you both authority, so they will not reach you; by Our signs, you two and those who follow you will be the victors."

* In this is evidence of Allah's favour upon His servant, in that Allah answered Musa's supplication; He said: ﴿سَنَشُدُّ عَضُدَكَ﴾.

* And in it: evidence that Allah gave Musa more than he asked, because he said: ﴿رِدْءًا يُصَدِّقُنِي إِنِّي أَخَافُ أَنْ يُكَذِّبُونِ﴾ [al-Qasas 28:34], and Allah gave him more than that, more than his being confirmed, by strengthening him as well; because confirmation means the report that he is truthful, but strengthening is more emphatic. Therefore He said: ﴿سَنَشُدُّ عَضُدَكَ بِأَخِيكَ﴾.

* And also: that Allah, the Exalted, may bestow favour upon the servant and make authority for him through the knowledge He has given him; by His words: ﴿وَنَجْعَلُ لَكُمَا سُلْطَانًا﴾ ﴿بِآيَاتِنَا﴾ [al-Qasas 28:35].

* And: knowledge is a weapon, because authority means strength and dominance, and when its cause is knowledge, this is evidence that knowledge is among the greatest weapons with which a person defends himself and argues. I think we passed the story of Ibn 'Umar with the servant (...), for had it not been for Ibn 'Umar's knowledge, this servant would have had authority; but Ibn 'Umar had of knowledge what gave him the power and dominance over that (...).

* And also, from the benefits of the verse: Allah the Exalted's protection of Musa and Harun; by His words: ﴿فَلَا يَصِلُونَ إِلَيْكُمَا﴾ [al-Qasas 28:35], and this is like His words: ﴿لَا تَخَافَا إِنَّنِي مَعَكُمَا أَسْمَعُ وَأَرَى﴾ [Ta-Ha 20:46] "Do not fear; indeed I am with you both, hearing and seeing."

* And also: that adherence to the law of Allah is a cause of victory. He said: ﴿أَنْتُمَا وَمَنِ اتَّبَعَكُمَا الْغَالِبُونَ﴾ [al-Qasas 28:35], everyone who follows you both.

(...) ﴿أَنْتُمَا وَمَنِ اتَّبَعَكُمَا الْغَالِبُونَ﴾.

* And among them: if this applies to the Children of Israel, that whoever follows Musa is victorious, then whoever follows the Prophet ﷺ is all the more so; for whoever follows the Prophet ﷺ is victorious. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿هُوَ الَّذِي أَرْسَلَ رَسُولَهُ بِالْهُدَى وَدِينِ الْحَقِّ لِيُظْهِرَهُ عَلَى الدِّينِ كُلِّهِ﴾ [al-Tawbah 9:33] "It is He who sent His Messenger with guidance and the religion of truth, to make it prevail over all religion." What is the meaning of ﴿لِيُظْهِرَهُ﴾?

Student: (...).

Shaykh: It makes it high (yu'alliyahu), because the root zhahr and zhuhur all indicates dominance.

He said: ﴿أَنْتُمَا وَمَنِ اتَّبَعَكُمَا الْغَالِبُونَ (٣٥) فَلَمَّا جَاءَهُمْ﴾ [al-Qasas 28:35-36].

Student: (...).

* * *

Shaykh: Then He said: ﴿فَلَمَّا جَاءَهُمْ مُوسَى بِآيَاتِنَا بَيِّنَاتٍ قَالُوا مَا هَذَا إِلَّا سِحْرٌ مُفْتَرًى وَمَا سَمِعْنَا بِهَذَا فِي آبَائِنَا الْأَوَّلِينَ﴾ [al-Qasas 28:36] "So when Musa came to them with Our clear signs, they said: 'This is nothing but fabricated magic, and we have not heard of this among our earlier forefathers.'"

* In this is derived: that Musa, peace be upon him, carried out what Allah sent him with.

* And among its benefits: that the signs which Allah sends with the prophets are clear and evident, so that the summoned people have no argument of obscurity in the proof; therefore Allah makes the signs clear and evident. And in the authentic hadith from the Prophet, peace be upon him: "There is no messenger except that Allah gave him what, similar to it, people believed; and what I was given is a revelation which Allah revealed to me, so I hope to be the most numerous of them in followers on the Day of Resurrection."[[Al-Bukhari (4981) with his chain from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Prophet ﷺ said: "There is no prophet among the prophets except that he was given what similar to it people believed in; and what I was given is a revelation which Allah revealed to me, so I hope to be the most numerous of them in followers on the Day of Resurrection."]] Therefore the signs with which the messengers are sent must be clear and evident, so that no argument remains for people.

* And also, from the benefits of the verse: the signs which Allah gave Musa were not one or two, but multiple signs, of the kind upon which human beings believe; but these people are stubborn tyrants, and we seek refuge in Allah.

* And among its benefits: the claim of those who deny the messengers is nothing but a form of obstinate denial. Their saying ﴿وَمَا سَمِعْنَا بِهَذَا فِي آبَائِنَا الْأَوَّلِينَ﴾ [al-Qasas 28:36], does it necessitate rejecting the truth or not?

Student: (...).

Shaykh: No. That does not necessitate rejecting the truth. That is, whatever you have heard, if it is true, then accept it. A person has no excuse if he says, "By God, we have never heard of this."

Among its benefits also: the enemies of the messengers give the messengers derogatory and defamatory titles, as shown by His words: ﴿This is nothing but fabricated magic﴾ [al-Qasas 36]. The enemies of the messengers have nothing but that they give them titles: "This is a magician, this is a liar, this is a madman, this is a poet," and the like.

So from this we also derive a related benefit: the enemies of the messengers will give those who call to the message of the messengers similar titles. They will say: "Reactionaries, backward, rigid, extremists, fanatics..." and the like. Yes, or perhaps they will go even further and say: "Misguided," as in His words: ﴿And when they saw them, they said, "Indeed, these are surely misguided"﴾ [al-Mutaffifin 32]. The point is that we must know that this call, the call to the truth, has enemies. These enemies who confronted the messengers with what they confronted them with, and the messengers were the strongest in leadership, will confront those who come after them with the same as, or more than, what they confronted them with. So let us reassure ourselves that if we call to Allah upon truth and insight, they will say things to us, and there will stand before us those who say to us what they said to the messengers.

Student: (...)?

Shaykh: Yes indeed, ﴿Our Lord, we have believed, so forgive us and have mercy upon us, and You are the best of the merciful﴾ [al-Mu'minun 109] (...), ﴿And when they saw them, they said, "Indeed, these are surely misguided"﴾ [al-Mutaffifin 32]. The point is that as long as the call is one, its enemy is one, and what was said of the first is said of the second.

Among the benefits of the verse: a person should not be deterred from speaking the truth by their rejection of it or by their describing him (...). Did Musa stop when they said this to him? No, he continued in the call, and the proof was established through him, even though he was threatened with prison. But peace be upon him did not care about this. Likewise, the caller to Allah should be patient as long as he knows he is upon the truth.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 28, verse 33–36 (part 1 of 3):

He said: ﴿And my brother Harun, he is more eloquent in tongue than me, so send him with me as a helper, to confirm me﴾ [al-Qasas 34].

First: What is the grammatical analysis (i'rab) of this sentence, ﴿And my brother Harun, he is more eloquent in tongue than me﴾?

﴿akhi (my brother)﴾ is a subject (mubtada'), or not? "Akhi" is the subject (mubtada').

The essential point is his saying: ﴿he is more eloquent in tongue than me﴾ [al-Qasas 34]. Then we ask: is ﴿huwa﴾ a pronoun of separation (damir al-fasl), or is ﴿huwa﴾ the subject (mubtada') and ﴿afsahu (more eloquent)﴾ the predicate (khabar), with the sentence serving as the predicate of the subject (...)? Because the pronoun of separation (...), and the subject and predicate are both definite (ma'rifatan); because in this case the predicate could be confused with a verb. But if the predicate is indefinite (nakirah), as here, then it is treated as the subject.

He said: ﴿And my brother Harun﴾ [al-Qasas 34]. Is he his brother from both mother and father, or from the father alone?

From both his mother and his father. As for the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿O son of my mother, do not seize me by my beard nor by my head﴾ [Ta-Ha 94], they mentioned that his attribution to his mother is because she is closer than the father, so he mentioned her (...) to make him feel compassion.

He said: ﴿And my brother Harun, he is more eloquent in tongue than me﴾ [al-Qasas 34].

﴿Afsah (more eloquent)﴾ means more clear (abyan) than me. His saying ﴿lisanan (in tongue)﴾ means speech (kalaman), and he expressed speech by "tongue" because it is the instrument of speech. Allah the Blessed and Exalted said: ﴿And We did not send any messenger except with the tongue of his people﴾ [Ibrahim 4], meaning with their speech and their language.

As for his saying ﴿more eloquent than me in tongue﴾, why? It has been said in the Isra'iliyyat (narrations from Israelite sources) that Musa, peace be upon him, had in his tongue (...) from a live coal he took and ate, when Pharaoh wanted to kill him, and his wife said: "He is a child who does not understand or know. If you want to test him, give him a date and a coal." So she presented to him the date and the coal; the coal was glittering and its appearance more beautiful than the date, so he took the coal and put it in his mouth, and his tongue became tied. This is an Isra'iliyyah, because this is not possible; for if he wanted to take the coal and took it, he could not hold it in his hand (...). For this reason Musa asked Allah to untie this knot, saying: ﴿And untie a knot from my tongue (27), that they may understand my speech﴾ [Ta-Ha 27, 28].

And you see some people who have a stammer in their tongue (fafa'ah), and some who have a lisp (ta'ta'ah) (...), and some who have neither this nor that, but cannot speak; you find that when he wants to speak—may Allah protect us—his face turns red and he gets tired (...). So the knot (ʿuqdah) is the same whether in the manner of the letters or in pronouncing the letter. Both are types of knots. In the manner of the letters: he cannot bring them out in their most complete form; or in the very act of pronunciation: he cannot, his tongue does not move freely.

So the correct view is that this defect in Musa, peace be upon him, was from the origin of his creation, and there was no date and coal.

He said: (﴿So send him with me as a helper﴾ [al-Qasas 34], a supporter (mu'in), and in one reading with a fathah on the dal without a hamzah), how do we say it? ﴿radan (a supporter)﴾, meaning (...) ﴿so send him with me as a helper (ridan)﴾.

Musa, peace be upon him, understood that Allah had sent him to Pharaoh from His saying: ﴿These two are proofs from your Lord to Pharaoh﴾ [al-Qasas 32]. For this reason he said: ﴿so send him with me﴾, and so here he knew that he was a messenger.

As for his saying ﴿ma'iya (with me)﴾, the "mi'iyyah" means companionship and accompaniment, and it is in each place according to what it is attached to, meaning according to what it is added to, and in each place it implies something different from what it implies in another place. So when it is said "the man is with his wife," it is not like when it is said "the commander is with his soldiers," or not? So there is a difference between them. Likewise when it is said "the milk is with the water," meaning mixed and blended with it. Here, ﴿so send him with me as a helper﴾ is not the companionship of a husband with his wife nor the companionship of milk with water; rather, it is an accompaniment intended for support and victory, and for this he said: ﴿ridan (a helper)﴾, and the ridf is the one who aids and backs a person.

﴿Yusaddiqunee (to confirm me)﴾: what is the meaning of ﴿yusaddiqunee﴾? It means that he would be one who confirms me before them, so that my words are strengthened by him and become true; and the meaning is not that he says, "You are truthful." Rather, when his speech strengthens my speech, that becomes a cause for their believing him.

He said: (In the jussive (bil-jazm) as the answer to the supplication; and in one reading in the nominative (bil-raf'), and its clause is a description (sifah) of ﴿ridan﴾).

(In the jussive): you say ﴿yusaddiqni﴾ is the answer to the supplication. Where is the supplication? ﴿so send him with me﴾, and this is clear, meaning: if you send him, he will confirm me.

(And in another reading): is this a Sab'i (canonical seven) reading or a shadhdh (irregular) one? Sab'i, because the author's rule, may Allah have mercy on him, is that when he says "in a reading" (fi qira'ah) it is Sab'i, and when he says "it was read" (wa-quri'a) it is shadhdh.

He said: ﴿So send him with me as a helper, to confirm me﴾, and its clause in the nominative reading is a description of ﴿ridan﴾, meaning: a helper confirming me. This is the detail.

* A student: (...)?
* The Shaykh: Yes, good. The benefit of the two readings (...) is a benefit, which is that his saying ﴿yusaddiqunee﴾, if it is the answer (to the request), then its meaning is that truthfulness is achieved through him; and if it is a description, then the meaning is that he tries to (...) or tries to show the people that he is truthful. So the nominative reading is by way of cause, and the jussive reading by way of result, so Harun is an active, influential agent.

He said: ﴿Indeed I fear that they will deny me﴾ [al-Qasas 34]. The pronoun in ﴿yukadhdhibun (they deny)﴾ is the plural waw pronoun referring to Pharaoh and his chiefs.

﴿Akhafu (I fear)﴾ means I expect and I dread, and it is not the fear of terror; there is no terror here, but he anticipates that and dreads it.

As for his saying ﴿an yukadhdhibun (that they deny)﴾, there is a difficulty in terms of grammar, because it is known that when ﴿an﴾ enters upon the five verbs (al-af'al al-khamsah), the nun is removed from them, and here there is a nun?

The answer: this nun is the nun of protection (nun al-waqayah), not the nun of inflection (nun al-i'rab), and for this you see it now with a kasrah. So the original is ("an yukadhdhibunanee") — the original is "yukadhdhibunanee," so the nun of the nominative was removed because of the accusative, and the ya was removed for lightness.

A parallel to it is His saying, the Exalted, in the same type in Surat al-Dhariyat: ﴿Indeed for those who did wrong is a portion like the portion of their companions, so let them not seek to hasten (fa-la yasta'jilun)﴾ [al-Dhariyat 59]. If you stop on it, you stop with sukun, so the beginner student who has no knowledge of grammar understands that here the nun remains with the presence of the prohibitive "la," and with the prohibitive "la" it must be removed. But we say: this nun in the verse is the nun of protection, as evidence that if you join it, you would make it kasrah and say: ﴿fa-la yasta'jilunee (59) fa-waylun﴾ [al-Dhariyat 59, 60]. Yes, is that so?

* A student: Yes.
* The Shaykh: Good. The author said, yes, Allah the Exalted said: (﴿We will strengthen your arm﴾ [al-Qasas 35], we will empower you).

Shadd (strengthening) means empowering, and the 'adud is the complete bone between the forearm and the shoulder; this is the 'adud, and strengthening the arm is a metaphor for empowerment, since the hand is the instrument of action; when its arm is strengthened and made firm, it becomes strong. The meaning is that We will empower you and support you with your brother ﴿We will strengthen your arm with your brother﴾ [al-Qasas 35], Harun. Did Allah answer his request or not? Allah answered his request, and said: ﴿We will strengthen﴾, and the sin (sin), what does it mean?

* A student: It indicates postponement (taswif).

* The Shaykh: Yes, it indicates postponement, but what do the grammarians say about its grammatical function?

* The student: (...).

* The Shaykh: For expansion (tanfis), which is for postponement; "sawfa" is for expansion, and it indicates strengthening of emphasis and proximity, the emphasis of a thing and bringing it near, that it will happen soon.

He said: ﴿We will strengthen your arm with your brother﴾. There is no doubt that when Allah says this to him, it means that he is being strengthened now, because Allah's promise is not merely to send Harun with him, but that he will be a helper to him in this matter.

(﴿And We will give you both authority﴾ [al-Qasas 35], domination), and this is a second glad tiding to both of them.

﴿And We will make﴾ is the counterpart of "for you both authority (sultanan)." The meaning of "sultan" here, the author says, is "domination (ghalabah)," and "sultan" in the Qur'an comes with the meaning of domination and power, and comes with the meaning of proof, because a person is strengthened by proof and has authority through it. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿You have no authority for this; do you say about Allah what you do not know?﴾ [Yunus 68]. What does ﴿you have no authority for this﴾ mean? It means: you have no proof for this. And His saying the Exalted: ﴿So pass through; you will not pass except with authority﴾ [al-Rahman 33], meaning with strength and domination. And His saying: ﴿His authority is only over those who take him as an ally﴾ [al-Nahl 100], meaning his control and domination.

Here he says: ﴿And We will give you both authority﴾ [al-Qasas 35], and says: (domination), so it is from the second category.

(﴿So they will not reach you both﴾ [al-Qasas 35] with harm): the meaning is that they will not reach you both with harm; so what you feared from them will be removed by what Allah has made for you of support through your brother. This is a glad tiding to both of them and serves to strengthen them, and it is similar to His saying the Exalted: ﴿Do not fear; indeed I am with you both, hearing and seeing﴾ [Ta-Ha 46].

The author said: (Go ﴿with Our signs﴾), it seems that the author sees that His saying ﴿with Our signs﴾ is separate from His saying ﴿And We will give you both authority﴾, and for this he estimated a verb for it to be attached to, and on this estimation the pause would be at His saying ﴿So they will not reach you both﴾, and we begin and say: ﴿with Our signs, you two and whoever follows you, are the victorious﴾ [al-Qasas 35].

Good, the author estimated (Go ﴿with Our signs﴾), then he also said (...) ﴿you two and whoever follows you are the victorious﴾, so the verse becomes, according to the author's estimation: ﴿And We will make for you both authority, so they will not reach you both﴾, ﴿with Our signs﴾, ﴿you two and whoever follows you are the victorious﴾; because he estimated (Go ﴿with Our signs﴾), and it is not appropriate to say ﴿you two and whoever follows you are the victorious﴾ as a continuation of it, because whoever followed them did not go with the signs. Do you understand, everyone?

* A student: Yes.

* The Shaykh: Good, this is one view.

Another view they say: His saying ﴿with Our signs﴾ is attached to ﴿And We will make﴾: "And We will make for you both authority with Our signs," meaning: because of Our signs We will make for you both authority, so they cannot reach you both nor nullify your call. On this, is there a need for an estimate in the verse or not?

* A student: No need.

* The Shaykh: No need for an estimate. And should we stop at His saying ﴿so they will not reach you both﴾ or continue? We continue, so the reading is: ﴿so they will not reach you both with Our signs﴾ [al-Qasas 35], meaning: because of the signs that you have. This meaning is the correct one. First: because it does not need an estimate, since an estimate, everyone, must be preceded by two stages: the first stage: establishing that there is an omission (hadhf) in the speech; the second stage: establishing that the estimated omitted element is this one, or not? (...) or another. The claim must be preceded by two stages: the first stage is establishing that there is an omission in the speech requiring explanation, and the second is establishing that the estimated element is this, meaning specifying the estimate; because even if we grant that the verse needs an estimate, it may be disputed, and it may be said to him: what is this estimate you have estimated? We do not grant that the estimate of the omitted element is this (...). Everyone who claims an omission in a verse needs two things or two stages: the first stage: establishing that there is an omission in the speech, and by what way do we know this? If the speech does not stand without an estimate, we know that there is an omission; this is one.

The second stage: establishing that the omitted element is this thing you estimated, since it is permissible that the estimate is something else, or not? And this is certainly an estimate determined by the context, because the context is what specifies the type of the omitted element.

Good, if the speech does not need this estimate, then it is better not to estimate. The meaning of this verse is very clear on the view of no estimate, and that the meaning is: We will make for you both authority by means of Our signs that are with you, so they will not reach you both; and this meaning is also clearer than what the author and others estimated, because in reality he says: ﴿with Our signs﴾ here is plural, and in the first he says: ﴿These two are proofs from your Lord to Pharaoh and his chiefs﴾ [al-Qasas 32]. So did Allah send them, when He sent them, with only one sign or with two signs? Two signs.

The correct view, then, is that the verse is connected, its parts joined to one another, and we read: ﴿so they will not reach you both with Our signs﴾, yes: ﴿And We will make for you both authority, so they will not reach you both with Our signs﴾, and it is attached to His saying: "We will make for you both authority with Our signs, so they will not reach you both."

Some of the grammarians claimed that His saying ﴿with Our signs﴾ is attached to ﴿the victorious﴾, and this in meaning is close to what we mentioned, meaning: "You two and whoever follows you are the victorious with Our signs." The one victorious by the signs is the one to whom authority was given through them, so on this view: "so they will not reach you both; you two and whoever follows you are the victorious with Our signs." Without doubt this is better than the author's estimate, because it needs no omission, and because it makes the speech connected in part to part; but there is an omission from the standpoint of grammatical rules, which is that ﴿the victorious﴾ is an active participle (ism fa'il), and the "al" attached to the active participle is, according to the grammarians, what? A relative pronoun:

"And a clear adjective, the ṣilah of (al) ..."

A relative pronoun, and it is known that a relative pronoun's complement does not operate on what precedes it; its complement does not govern, so we then need an answer to this rule.

The answer they gave: the "al" here is not relative, but like the "al" that enters on a fixed noun, entering on "the man" and "the lion" and similar.

So in this estimate there is a violation of the known grammatical rules.

We return now to the view that the correct approach is to make His saying ﴿with Our signs﴾ attached to ﴿And We will make for you both authority﴾, and we are spared all that: the violations, the estimates we rely on, and the specification of the estimated element.

And His saying ﴿with Our signs﴾, ﴿so they will not reach you both with Our signs﴾, contains evidence that Allah the Exalted gave Musa and Harun signs; and He mentioned in another surah that He gave him nine signs, or not? ﴿And We certainly gave Musa nine clear signs, so ask the Children of Israel when he came to them﴾ [al-Isra' 101].

And His saying ﴿you two and whoever follows you﴾: who are they? From the Children of Israel and from the family of Pharaoh, because among the family of Pharaoh were those who followed them, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And a believing man from the family of Pharaoh said﴾ [Ghafir 28].

And His saying ﴿and whoever follows you﴾ contains evidence that a person is aided and made victorious by following the messengers, and that there is no path to victory and dominance except entering the path of the messengers and following them. Accordingly, there is from this a rule: whoever is more closely following the Messenger is nearer to victory, and whoever is further from following the Messenger is further from victory; because it is known among the established rules that when a ruling is attached to an attribute, its establishment is in strength and weakness, existence and non-existence, according to that attribute. When a ruling is attached to an attribute, the establishment of the ruling is in existence and non-existence, strength and weakness, according to that attribute, understood?

For example: ﴿Indeed Allah is with the patient﴾ [al-Baqarah 153]: His companionship with the patient is in strength and weakness according to the patience they have.

﴿Indeed Allah is with those who are mindful of Him﴾ [al-Nahl 128]: the existence of companionship for the God-conscious is in strength and weakness according to their God-consciousness... and so on.

The Shaykh (Ibn 'Uthaymin) said, in his commentary on Allah's words:

﴿أَنْتُمَا وَمَنِ اتَّبَعَكُمَا الْغَالِبُونَ﴾ [al-Qasas 28:35] "You two and those who follow you will be the victors." **Al-ghalibun** (the victors): over whom? The author says: "(the victors) over them." ... But if we want to take this in its general sense, we say: ﴿أَنْتُمَا وَمَنِ اتَّبَعَكُمَا الْغَالِبُونَ﴾ means victorious over those who oppose them. The followers of the messengers are victorious over those who oppose the messengers, always and forever, or not? Always and forever. Indeed, these matters (...) over others. The Prophet ﷺ said: "I have been helped with terror (of my enemy) for a distance of one month."[[Agreed upon (Muttafaqun 'alayh). Al-Bukhari (438) and Muslim (521/3), from the hadith of Jabir ibn 'Abdullah, may Allah be pleased with him and his father.]] Allahu akbar! How great this benefit is, if only we were at the level we should be! If we truly followed this noble Prophet ﷺ in reality, our enemy would be terrified of us for a distance of one month. But, unfortunately, we were not truly following the Messenger, peace be upon him, in reality. Therefore our might has become between ourselves, neither those who claim Islam among us, nor those who wish to shelter under the principle of jahiliyyah, which is Arab nationalism (al-qawmiyyah al-'arabiyyah). Nationalism has not triumphed since its emergence until today, and it will never triumph. Rather, it only increases in failure, division and fragmentation, and indeed, fighting among its own. Likewise, in reality, we have not united on an Islamic nationality; we have not united on it. So the Muslims remain neither on this nor on that, and therefore we did not have the victory which Allah promised to His Prophet ﷺ.

He said: (﴿فَلَمَّا جَاءَهُمْ مُوسَى بِآيَاتِنَا بَيِّنَاتٍ﴾ [al-Qasas 28:36] clear, as a circumstantial state (hal)).

﴿فَلَمَّا جَاءَهُمْ﴾ means: the people of Pharaoh (Ali Fir'awn).

﴿مُوسَى بِآيَاتِنَا﴾: He did not say "and Harun," because the messengership originally belonged to Musa.

As for ﴿بِآيَاتِنَا﴾, the letter ba' indicates accompaniment, meaning accompanied by the signs.

﴿بِآيَاتِنَا﴾ is the plural of ayah, which means signs. It is attributed to Allah as the attribution of a gift to its giver, because these signs are not signs upon Allah; rather they are signs from Him, upon what? Upon the messengership of Musa, and Musa, within it, is proof that Allah alone is the true God.

﴿بِآيَاتِنَا بَيِّنَاتٍ﴾: He said "clear," and regarding its i'rab (grammatical analysis) he said: "a circumstantial state (hal)." A hal of what? (...)

Student: Of (ayat).

Shaykh: Of (ayat). And it is not correct to be an adjective (sifah)?

Student: (...)

Shaykh: Is it correct or not correct? Give me the ruling before the reason.

Student: It is not correct.

Shaykh: It is not correct, because (ayat) is definite (ma'rifah), and ﴿بَيِّنَاتٍ﴾ is indefinite (nakirah), and a definite noun is not described by an indefinite noun. Rather, when an indefinite noun comes after a definite noun and is its description, it is parsed as a hal.

In His words ﴿بِآيَاتِنَا بَيِّنَاتٍ﴾ there is an establishment of proof, because an ayah is a sign, and whenever it is more evident, the proof is stronger. So the signs are clear.

He brought them the clear signs, so what answer came from them?

(﴿قَالُوا مَا هَذَا إِلَّا سِحْرٌ مُفْتَرًى﴾ [al-Qasas 28:36] fabricated (mukhtalaq)). I seek refuge in Allah.

﴿مَا هَذَا﴾ means: what you have brought, O Musa, ﴿إِلَّا سِحْرٌ﴾. Here we ask: why did "ma" not act like "laysa," although the dialect of the Hijaz makes it act like "laysa"? Because Ibn Malik says?

Student: (...)

Shaykh: Yes. Its meaning is that the negation must remain, and here the negation did not remain, so it was nullified by (...)

Their saying ﴿مَا هَذَا إِلَّا سِحْرٌ مُفْتَرًى﴾: what is the magic they meant (...)?

Student: The staff.

Shaykh: The staff and the hand. This is if we say that it refers to the sensory signs. But if we say that it refers to the non-sensory signs, which are like speech, then the Prophet, peace be upon him, said: "Indeed, some eloquence is magic."[[Narrated by al-Bukhari (5767), from the hadith of 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with him and his father.]]

As for His words (﴿مُفْتَرًى﴾ fabricated (mukhtalaq)): the attribution of fabrication to the speech is clear, but the attribution of fabrication to the staff and the hand? Because magic does not truly change things; it changes them only in imagination, according to what a person imagines. So is this imagining in agreement with reality or contrary to reality? And everything that contradicts reality is fabricated; everything that contradicts reality is fabricated. Take care, O people.

So, the fabrication here, if it is attributed to what they said of the message, is problematic.

Student: (...)

Shaykh: Clear. If it is attributed to what they said of the message, is it problematic or clear? It is clear, because attributing fabrication to speech is a known matter. But if it is attributed to what he brought of sensory signs, such as the transformation of the staff and the hand emerging white, then how can we say it is fabricated? Because magic does not turn a matter from its reality; it does not change it from its reality. So its appearance in a state other than its true one is a kind of lying and calumny. Therefore they said: ﴿إِلَّا سِحْرٌ مُفْتَرًى﴾.

(﴿وَمَا سَمِعْنَا بِهَذَا﴾ present (ka'innan) ﴿فِي﴾ the days of ﴿آبَائِنَا الْأَوَّلِينَ﴾ [al-Qasas 28:36]) (...)

﴿وَمَا سَمِعْنَا بِهَذَا فِي آبَائِنَا الْأَوَّلِينَ﴾.

﴿وَمَا سَمِعْنَا بِهَذَا﴾: the referent of "this" is what he brought of the message, because it is what is heard; as for the sign of the hand and the staff, it is witnessed and seen.

As for His words ﴿فِي آبَائِنَا﴾, the commentator, the author, said: "present (ka'innan)," indicating that the complement of the prepositional phrase with ﴿آبَائِنَا الْأَوَّلِينَ﴾ is omitted, its estimate being "present."

Is "present (ka'innan)" here, according to the author's estimate, a second object or a circumstantial state?

A circumstantial state of the demonstrative.

As for His words ﴿فِي آبَائِنَا الْأَوَّلِينَ﴾, it means: in their time, and therefore he said: "in the days of our first forefathers," meaning the earlier ones.

Is their statement true or false?

Student: False.

Shaykh: And why would they lie?

Student: (...) ﴿وَلَقَدْ جَاءَكُمْ يُوسُفُ مِنْ قَبْلُ﴾.

Shaykh: Yes: ﴿بِالْبَيِّنَاتِ فَمَا زِلْتُمْ فِي شَكٍّ مِمَّا جَاءَكُمْ بِهِ حَتَّى إِذَا هَلَكَ قُلْتُمْ لَنْ يَبْعَثَ اللَّهُ مِنْ بَعْدِهِ رَسُولًا﴾ [Ghafir 40:34] "with clear proofs; but you remained in doubt about what he brought you, until, when he died, you said: 'Allah will never send after him a messenger.'"

So their saying ﴿وَمَا سَمِعْنَا بِهَذَا فِي آبَائِنَا الْأَوَّلِينَ﴾ [al-Qasas 28:36] is a false report, and they are liars in this claim. Then, supposing the claim is true and they had not heard of it, does the fact that this did not exist among the earlier ones necessitate that it is false for the later ones?

Student: It does not necessitate it.

Shaykh: It does not necessitate it, because when the truth comes, it must be accepted, whether or not it existed among the earlier ones. So this argument is composed of falsehood and nonsense: as for the falsehood, their saying ﴿وَمَا سَمِعْنَا بِهَذَا فِي آبَائِنَا الْأَوَّلِينَ﴾ is a lie, because their believer had established proof against them by the existence of a parallel to what Musa brought, in His words: ﴿وَلَقَدْ جَاءَكُمْ يُوسُفُ مِنْ قَبْلُ بِالْبَيِّنَاتِ﴾. As for it being a false argument on the assumption that it is true in its statement, it is because the absence of that among the earlier ones does not necessitate the falsity of its existence among the later ones, for Allah, the Exalted, does what He wills. So as long as the signs are clear, there is no proof in that they did not occur before.

As for His words ﴿فِي آبَائِنَا الْأَوَّلِينَ﴾: how can he say ﴿الْأَوَّلِينَ﴾ when they are fathers?

Because "father" (ab) is applied to the direct father and to the grandfather, however far up. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿مِلَّةَ أَبِيكُمْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ هُوَ سَمَّاكُمُ﴾ [al-Hajj 22:78] "the religion of your father Ibrahim; He named you..." And Yusuf said: ﴿وَاتَّبَعْتُ مِلَّةَ آبَائِي إِبْرَاهِيمَ وَإِسْحَاقَ وَيَعْقُوبَ﴾ [Yusuf 12:38] "And I followed the religion of my forefathers, Ibrahim, Ishaq and Ya'qub." Ya'qub was his direct father, Ishaq was his grandfather, and Ibrahim was his grandfather's father. He called them fathers. Although this involves the principle of prominence (taghlib), in ﴿مِلَّةَ أَبِيكُمْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ﴾ there is no prominence, meaning there is no direct father in it. Therefore the preferred view regarding (...) is that the grandfather...

Student: He blocks the grandfather.

Shaykh: He blocks the grandfather, and that Allah...

Student: (...)?

Shaykh: This is specific to the apparent sense. But ﴿ومَا سَمِعْنَا بِهَذَا﴾ [al-Qasas 28:36] (...)

* * *

From this is derived: the permissibility of offering an excuse when commanded to do something, in order to be released from (...). Yes, even in obeying the ruler, for example: if he commands you to do something, obedience to him is obligatory in what is not sinful, and there is no harm in mentioning an excuse in order to be exempted from this command, just as the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, used to present excuses to the Prophet ﷺ when he commanded them to do something, so that he would excuse them.

* And it is derived from it that natural fear does not contradict the station of messengership, by His words: ﴿فَأَخَافُ أَنْ يَقْتُلُونِ﴾ [al-Qasas 28:33] "I fear that they will kill me."

* And it is derived from it that retaliation (qisas) existed in earlier times (...), existing among the previous nations; by His words: ﴿فَأَخَافُ أَنْ يَقْتُلُونِ﴾, meaning in exchange for his killing (...). So do we say that this was by way of retaliation, or by way of aggression from the family of Pharaoh? That is, they may not have cared. If we applied this to the Islamic ruling it would be deficient, because a Muslim is not killed for a disbeliever. So we say: this, His words ﴿فَأَخَافُ أَنْ يَقْتُلُونِ﴾, is either because retaliation was well known among them, or because he feared they would attack him with killing, even if that was not by right. And as long as it is a possibility, it cannot be taken as evidence for (...).

* * *

﴿وَأَخِي هَارُونُ هُوَ أَفْصَحُ مِنِّي لِسَانًا﴾, what?

Student: (...)?

Shaykh: Same, (...).

He said: ﴿وَأَخِي هَارُونُ هُوَ أَفْصَحُ مِنِّي لِسَانًا فَأَرْسِلْهُ مَعِيَ رِدْءًا يُصَدِّقُنِي إِنِّي أَخَافُ أَنْ يُكَذِّبُونِ﴾ [al-Qasas 28:34] "And my brother Harun is more eloquent in tongue than I, so send him with me as a helper to confirm me; indeed, I fear that they will deny me."

* From this is derived: the great favour of Musa toward his brother, in that Allah the Exalted made it so that He sent him with him. Therefore it is said: the greatest gift a beloved gave to his beloved is that which Musa gave to Harun, because he asked Allah to send him with him, and messengership is a great station which none attains except the choicest of the sons of Adam.

Student: (...).

Shaykh: * And also among the benefits, from the benefits of the verse: it is permissible for a person to seek help from others in calling to Allah, the Exalted; by His words: ﴿فَأَرْسِلْهُ مَعِيَ رِدْءًا﴾ [al-Qasas 28:34].

* And also: that taking helpers is one of the causes of success, and this is a known matter from ancient times and modern, that whenever a person has someone with him who helps and supports him, that is closer to his success than being alone. The common people say: "one hand does not clap."

* And among them: eloquence has an effect; eloquence of tongue has a strong effect on acceptance or rejection. The Prophet ﷺ said: "Indeed, some eloquence is magic,"[[Narrated by al-Bukhari (5767), from the hadith of 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar.]] by His words: ﴿هُوَ أَفْصَحُ مِنِّي لِسَانًا﴾.

* And among them: the virtue of Musa, peace be upon him, by his acknowledgment of his brother's superiority: ﴿هُوَ أَفْصَحُ مِنِّي لِسَانًا﴾, because some people are deficient but cannot express the perfection of others while acknowledging their own deficiency.

* And among its benefits: that the caller should mention the justifications for his call, because his saying ﴿هُوَ أَفْصَحُ مِنِّي لِسَانًا فَأَرْسِلْهُ﴾ [al-Qasas 28:34] is one of the justifications for his call and his request that Allah, blessed and exalted, send him with him, namely that he is more eloquent in tongue. This is known (...) among the etiquette of callers, that a person mentions the justifications of the call, saying: "By Allah (...)."

* And also, from the noble verses: Musa, peace be upon him, feared that they would deny him if he were alone, so he sought further help, because, as we said, one with another is closer to being believed.

* And also from it: that a report becomes more firmly established by the multiplicity of its reporters, or not?

Student: (...).

Shaykh: Yes.

Student: He said (...).

Shaykh: Yes, not (...).

Student: (...)?

Shaykh: (...) helps him; because the essence of messengership is a report, so if he has with him someone who strengthens this report, confirms it and validates it, it becomes stronger. And the establishment of a report by the multiplicity of its reporters is also a known matter, but (...).

* * *

﴿قَالَ سَنَشُدُّ عَضُدَكَ بِأَخِيكَ وَنَجْعَلُ لَكُمَا سُلْطَانًا فَلَا يَصِلُونَ إِلَيْكُمَا بِآيَاتِنَا أَنْتُمَا وَمَنِ اتَّبَعَكُمَا الْغَالِبُونَ﴾ [al-Qasas 28:35] "He said: We will strengthen your arm through your brother, and We will give you both authority, so they will not reach you; by Our signs, you two and those who follow you will be the victors."

* In this is evidence of Allah's favour upon His servant, in that Allah answered Musa's supplication; He said: ﴿سَنَشُدُّ عَضُدَكَ﴾.

* And in it: evidence that Allah gave Musa more than he asked, because he said: ﴿رِدْءًا يُصَدِّقُنِي إِنِّي أَخَافُ أَنْ يُكَذِّبُونِ﴾ [al-Qasas 28:34], and Allah gave him more than that, more than his being confirmed, by strengthening him as well; because confirmation means the report that he is truthful, but strengthening is more emphatic. Therefore He said: ﴿سَنَشُدُّ عَضُدَكَ بِأَخِيكَ﴾.

* And also: that Allah, the Exalted, may bestow favour upon the servant and make authority for him through the knowledge He has given him; by His words: ﴿وَنَجْعَلُ لَكُمَا سُلْطَانًا﴾ ﴿بِآيَاتِنَا﴾ [al-Qasas 28:35].

* And: knowledge is a weapon, because authority means strength and dominance, and when its cause is knowledge, this is evidence that knowledge is among the greatest weapons with which a person defends himself and argues. I think we passed the story of Ibn 'Umar with the servant (...), for had it not been for Ibn 'Umar's knowledge, this servant would have had authority; but Ibn 'Umar had of knowledge what gave him the power and dominance over that (...).

* And also, from the benefits of the verse: Allah the Exalted's protection of Musa and Harun; by His words: ﴿فَلَا يَصِلُونَ إِلَيْكُمَا﴾ [al-Qasas 28:35], and this is like His words: ﴿لَا تَخَافَا إِنَّنِي مَعَكُمَا أَسْمَعُ وَأَرَى﴾ [Ta-Ha 20:46] "Do not fear; indeed I am with you both, hearing and seeing."

* And also: that adherence to the law of Allah is a cause of victory. He said: ﴿أَنْتُمَا وَمَنِ اتَّبَعَكُمَا الْغَالِبُونَ﴾ [al-Qasas 28:35], everyone who follows you both.

(...) ﴿أَنْتُمَا وَمَنِ اتَّبَعَكُمَا الْغَالِبُونَ﴾.

* And among them: if this applies to the Children of Israel, that whoever follows Musa is victorious, then whoever follows the Prophet ﷺ is all the more so; for whoever follows the Prophet ﷺ is victorious. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿هُوَ الَّذِي أَرْسَلَ رَسُولَهُ بِالْهُدَى وَدِينِ الْحَقِّ لِيُظْهِرَهُ عَلَى الدِّينِ كُلِّهِ﴾ [al-Tawbah 9:33] "It is He who sent His Messenger with guidance and the religion of truth, to make it prevail over all religion." What is the meaning of ﴿لِيُظْهِرَهُ﴾?

Student: (...).

Shaykh: It makes it high (yu'alliyahu), because the root zhahr and zhuhur all indicates dominance.

He said: ﴿أَنْتُمَا وَمَنِ اتَّبَعَكُمَا الْغَالِبُونَ (٣٥) فَلَمَّا جَاءَهُمْ﴾ [al-Qasas 28:35-36].

Student: (...).

* * *

Shaykh: Then He said: ﴿فَلَمَّا جَاءَهُمْ مُوسَى بِآيَاتِنَا بَيِّنَاتٍ قَالُوا مَا هَذَا إِلَّا سِحْرٌ مُفْتَرًى وَمَا سَمِعْنَا بِهَذَا فِي آبَائِنَا الْأَوَّلِينَ﴾ [al-Qasas 28:36] "So when Musa came to them with Our clear signs, they said: 'This is nothing but fabricated magic, and we have not heard of this among our earlier forefathers.'"

* In this is derived: that Musa, peace be upon him, carried out what Allah sent him with.

* And among its benefits: that the signs which Allah sends with the prophets are clear and evident, so that the summoned people have no argument of obscurity in the proof; therefore Allah makes the signs clear and evident. And in the authentic hadith from the Prophet, peace be upon him: "There is no messenger except that Allah gave him what, similar to it, people believed; and what I was given is a revelation which Allah revealed to me, so I hope to be the most numerous of them in followers on the Day of Resurrection."[[Al-Bukhari (4981) with his chain from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Prophet ﷺ said: "There is no prophet among the prophets except that he was given what similar to it people believed in; and what I was given is a revelation which Allah revealed to me, so I hope to be the most numerous of them in followers on the Day of Resurrection."]] Therefore the signs with which the messengers are sent must be clear and evident, so that no argument remains for people.

* And also, from the benefits of the verse: the signs which Allah gave Musa were not one or two, but multiple signs, of the kind upon which human beings believe; but these people are stubborn tyrants, and we seek refuge in Allah.

* And among its benefits: the claim of those who deny the messengers is nothing but a form of obstinate denial. Their saying ﴿وَمَا سَمِعْنَا بِهَذَا فِي آبَائِنَا الْأَوَّلِينَ﴾ [al-Qasas 28:36], does it necessitate rejecting the truth or not?

Student: (...).

Shaykh: No. That does not necessitate rejecting the truth. That is, whatever you have heard, if it is true, then accept it. A person has no excuse if he says, "By God, we have never heard of this."

Among its benefits also: the enemies of the messengers give the messengers derogatory and defamatory titles, as shown by His words: ﴿This is nothing but fabricated magic﴾ [al-Qasas 36]. The enemies of the messengers have nothing but that they give them titles: "This is a magician, this is a liar, this is a madman, this is a poet," and the like.

So from this we also derive a related benefit: the enemies of the messengers will give those who call to the message of the messengers similar titles. They will say: "Reactionaries, backward, rigid, extremists, fanatics..." and the like. Yes, or perhaps they will go even further and say: "Misguided," as in His words: ﴿And when they saw them, they said, "Indeed, these are surely misguided"﴾ [al-Mutaffifin 32]. The point is that we must know that this call, the call to the truth, has enemies. These enemies who confronted the messengers with what they confronted them with, and the messengers were the strongest in leadership, will confront those who come after them with the same as, or more than, what they confronted them with. So let us reassure ourselves that if we call to Allah upon truth and insight, they will say things to us, and there will stand before us those who say to us what they said to the messengers.

Student: (...)?

Shaykh: Yes indeed, ﴿Our Lord, we have believed, so forgive us and have mercy upon us, and You are the best of the merciful﴾ [al-Mu'minun 109] (...), ﴿And when they saw them, they said, "Indeed, these are surely misguided"﴾ [al-Mutaffifin 32]. The point is that as long as the call is one, its enemy is one, and what was said of the first is said of the second.

Among the benefits of the verse: a person should not be deterred from speaking the truth by their rejection of it or by their describing him (...). Did Musa stop when they said this to him? No, he continued in the call, and the proof was established through him, even though he was threatened with prison. But peace be upon him did not care about this. Likewise, the caller to Allah should be patient as long as he knows he is upon the truth.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 28, verse 33–36 (part 1 of 3):

He said: ﴿And my brother Harun, he is more eloquent in tongue than me, so send him with me as a helper, to confirm me﴾ [al-Qasas 34].

First: What is the grammatical analysis (i'rab) of this sentence, ﴿And my brother Harun, he is more eloquent in tongue than me﴾?

﴿akhi (my brother)﴾ is a subject (mubtada'), or not? "Akhi" is the subject (mubtada').

The essential point is his saying: ﴿he is more eloquent in tongue than me﴾ [al-Qasas 34]. Then we ask: is ﴿huwa﴾ a pronoun of separation (damir al-fasl), or is ﴿huwa﴾ the subject (mubtada') and ﴿afsahu (more eloquent)﴾ the predicate (khabar), with the sentence serving as the predicate of the subject (...)? Because the pronoun of separation (...), and the subject and predicate are both definite (ma'rifatan); because in this case the predicate could be confused with a verb. But if the predicate is indefinite (nakirah), as here, then it is treated as the subject.

He said: ﴿And my brother Harun﴾ [al-Qasas 34]. Is he his brother from both mother and father, or from the father alone?

From both his mother and his father. As for the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿O son of my mother, do not seize me by my beard nor by my head﴾ [Ta-Ha 94], they mentioned that his attribution to his mother is because she is closer than the father, so he mentioned her (...) to make him feel compassion.

He said: ﴿And my brother Harun, he is more eloquent in tongue than me﴾ [al-Qasas 34].

﴿Afsah (more eloquent)﴾ means more clear (abyan) than me. His saying ﴿lisanan (in tongue)﴾ means speech (kalaman), and he expressed speech by "tongue" because it is the instrument of speech. Allah the Blessed and Exalted said: ﴿And We did not send any messenger except with the tongue of his people﴾ [Ibrahim 4], meaning with their speech and their language.

As for his saying ﴿more eloquent than me in tongue﴾, why? It has been said in the Isra'iliyyat (narrations from Israelite sources) that Musa, peace be upon him, had in his tongue (...) from a live coal he took and ate, when Pharaoh wanted to kill him, and his wife said: "He is a child who does not understand or know. If you want to test him, give him a date and a coal." So she presented to him the date and the coal; the coal was glittering and its appearance more beautiful than the date, so he took the coal and put it in his mouth, and his tongue became tied. This is an Isra'iliyyah, because this is not possible; for if he wanted to take the coal and took it, he could not hold it in his hand (...). For this reason Musa asked Allah to untie this knot, saying: ﴿And untie a knot from my tongue (27), that they may understand my speech﴾ [Ta-Ha 27, 28].

And you see some people who have a stammer in their tongue (fafa'ah), and some who have a lisp (ta'ta'ah) (...), and some who have neither this nor that, but cannot speak; you find that when he wants to speak—may Allah protect us—his face turns red and he gets tired (...). So the knot (ʿuqdah) is the same whether in the manner of the letters or in pronouncing the letter. Both are types of knots. In the manner of the letters: he cannot bring them out in their most complete form; or in the very act of pronunciation: he cannot, his tongue does not move freely.

So the correct view is that this defect in Musa, peace be upon him, was from the origin of his creation, and there was no date and coal.

He said: (﴿So send him with me as a helper﴾ [al-Qasas 34], a supporter (mu'in), and in one reading with a fathah on the dal without a hamzah), how do we say it? ﴿radan (a supporter)﴾, meaning (...) ﴿so send him with me as a helper (ridan)﴾.

Musa, peace be upon him, understood that Allah had sent him to Pharaoh from His saying: ﴿These two are proofs from your Lord to Pharaoh﴾ [al-Qasas 32]. For this reason he said: ﴿so send him with me﴾, and so here he knew that he was a messenger.

As for his saying ﴿ma'iya (with me)﴾, the "mi'iyyah" means companionship and accompaniment, and it is in each place according to what it is attached to, meaning according to what it is added to, and in each place it implies something different from what it implies in another place. So when it is said "the man is with his wife," it is not like when it is said "the commander is with his soldiers," or not? So there is a difference between them. Likewise when it is said "the milk is with the water," meaning mixed and blended with it. Here, ﴿so send him with me as a helper﴾ is not the companionship of a husband with his wife nor the companionship of milk with water; rather, it is an accompaniment intended for support and victory, and for this he said: ﴿ridan (a helper)﴾, and the ridf is the one who aids and backs a person.

﴿Yusaddiqunee (to confirm me)﴾: what is the meaning of ﴿yusaddiqunee﴾? It means that he would be one who confirms me before them, so that my words are strengthened by him and become true; and the meaning is not that he says, "You are truthful." Rather, when his speech strengthens my speech, that becomes a cause for their believing him.

He said: (In the jussive (bil-jazm) as the answer to the supplication; and in one reading in the nominative (bil-raf'), and its clause is a description (sifah) of ﴿ridan﴾).

(In the jussive): you say ﴿yusaddiqni﴾ is the answer to the supplication. Where is the supplication? ﴿so send him with me﴾, and this is clear, meaning: if you send him, he will confirm me.

(And in another reading): is this a Sab'i (canonical seven) reading or a shadhdh (irregular) one? Sab'i, because the author's rule, may Allah have mercy on him, is that when he says "in a reading" (fi qira'ah) it is Sab'i, and when he says "it was read" (wa-quri'a) it is shadhdh.

He said: ﴿So send him with me as a helper, to confirm me﴾, and its clause in the nominative reading is a description of ﴿ridan﴾, meaning: a helper confirming me. This is the detail.

* A student: (...)?
* The Shaykh: Yes, good. The benefit of the two readings (...) is a benefit, which is that his saying ﴿yusaddiqunee﴾, if it is the answer (to the request), then its meaning is that truthfulness is achieved through him; and if it is a description, then the meaning is that he tries to (...) or tries to show the people that he is truthful. So the nominative reading is by way of cause, and the jussive reading by way of result, so Harun is an active, influential agent.

He said: ﴿Indeed I fear that they will deny me﴾ [al-Qasas 34]. The pronoun in ﴿yukadhdhibun (they deny)﴾ is the plural waw pronoun referring to Pharaoh and his chiefs.

﴿Akhafu (I fear)﴾ means I expect and I dread, and it is not the fear of terror; there is no terror here, but he anticipates that and dreads it.

As for his saying ﴿an yukadhdhibun (that they deny)﴾, there is a difficulty in terms of grammar, because it is known that when ﴿an﴾ enters upon the five verbs (al-af'al al-khamsah), the nun is removed from them, and here there is a nun?

The answer: this nun is the nun of protection (nun al-waqayah), not the nun of inflection (nun al-i'rab), and for this you see it now with a kasrah. So the original is ("an yukadhdhibunanee") — the original is "yukadhdhibunanee," so the nun of the nominative was removed because of the accusative, and the ya was removed for lightness.

A parallel to it is His saying, the Exalted, in the same type in Surat al-Dhariyat: ﴿Indeed for those who did wrong is a portion like the portion of their companions, so let them not seek to hasten (fa-la yasta'jilun)﴾ [al-Dhariyat 59]. If you stop on it, you stop with sukun, so the beginner student who has no knowledge of grammar understands that here the nun remains with the presence of the prohibitive "la," and with the prohibitive "la" it must be removed. But we say: this nun in the verse is the nun of protection, as evidence that if you join it, you would make it kasrah and say: ﴿fa-la yasta'jilunee (59) fa-waylun﴾ [al-Dhariyat 59, 60]. Yes, is that so?

* A student: Yes.
* The Shaykh: Good. The author said, yes, Allah the Exalted said: (﴿We will strengthen your arm﴾ [al-Qasas 35], we will empower you).

Shadd (strengthening) means empowering, and the 'adud is the complete bone between the forearm and the shoulder; this is the 'adud, and strengthening the arm is a metaphor for empowerment, since the hand is the instrument of action; when its arm is strengthened and made firm, it becomes strong. The meaning is that We will empower you and support you with your brother ﴿We will strengthen your arm with your brother﴾ [al-Qasas 35], Harun. Did Allah answer his request or not? Allah answered his request, and said: ﴿We will strengthen﴾, and the sin (sin), what does it mean?

* A student: It indicates postponement (taswif).

* The Shaykh: Yes, it indicates postponement, but what do the grammarians say about its grammatical function?

* The student: (...).

* The Shaykh: For expansion (tanfis), which is for postponement; "sawfa" is for expansion, and it indicates strengthening of emphasis and proximity, the emphasis of a thing and bringing it near, that it will happen soon.

He said: ﴿We will strengthen your arm with your brother﴾. There is no doubt that when Allah says this to him, it means that he is being strengthened now, because Allah's promise is not merely to send Harun with him, but that he will be a helper to him in this matter.

(﴿And We will give you both authority﴾ [al-Qasas 35], domination), and this is a second glad tiding to both of them.

﴿And We will make﴾ is the counterpart of "for you both authority (sultanan)." The meaning of "sultan" here, the author says, is "domination (ghalabah)," and "sultan" in the Qur'an comes with the meaning of domination and power, and comes with the meaning of proof, because a person is strengthened by proof and has authority through it. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿You have no authority for this; do you say about Allah what you do not know?﴾ [Yunus 68]. What does ﴿you have no authority for this﴾ mean? It means: you have no proof for this. And His saying the Exalted: ﴿So pass through; you will not pass except with authority﴾ [al-Rahman 33], meaning with strength and domination. And His saying: ﴿His authority is only over those who take him as an ally﴾ [al-Nahl 100], meaning his control and domination.

Here he says: ﴿And We will give you both authority﴾ [al-Qasas 35], and says: (domination), so it is from the second category.

(﴿So they will not reach you both﴾ [al-Qasas 35] with harm): the meaning is that they will not reach you both with harm; so what you feared from them will be removed by what Allah has made for you of support through your brother. This is a glad tiding to both of them and serves to strengthen them, and it is similar to His saying the Exalted: ﴿Do not fear; indeed I am with you both, hearing and seeing﴾ [Ta-Ha 46].

The author said: (Go ﴿with Our signs﴾), it seems that the author sees that His saying ﴿with Our signs﴾ is separate from His saying ﴿And We will give you both authority﴾, and for this he estimated a verb for it to be attached to, and on this estimation the pause would be at His saying ﴿So they will not reach you both﴾, and we begin and say: ﴿with Our signs, you two and whoever follows you, are the victorious﴾ [al-Qasas 35].

Good, the author estimated (Go ﴿with Our signs﴾), then he also said (...) ﴿you two and whoever follows you are the victorious﴾, so the verse becomes, according to the author's estimation: ﴿And We will make for you both authority, so they will not reach you both﴾, ﴿with Our signs﴾, ﴿you two and whoever follows you are the victorious﴾; because he estimated (Go ﴿with Our signs﴾), and it is not appropriate to say ﴿you two and whoever follows you are the victorious﴾ as a continuation of it, because whoever followed them did not go with the signs. Do you understand, everyone?

* A student: Yes.

* The Shaykh: Good, this is one view.

Another view they say: His saying ﴿with Our signs﴾ is attached to ﴿And We will make﴾: "And We will make for you both authority with Our signs," meaning: because of Our signs We will make for you both authority, so they cannot reach you both nor nullify your call. On this, is there a need for an estimate in the verse or not?

* A student: No need.

* The Shaykh: No need for an estimate. And should we stop at His saying ﴿so they will not reach you both﴾ or continue? We continue, so the reading is: ﴿so they will not reach you both with Our signs﴾ [al-Qasas 35], meaning: because of the signs that you have. This meaning is the correct one. First: because it does not need an estimate, since an estimate, everyone, must be preceded by two stages: the first stage: establishing that there is an omission (hadhf) in the speech; the second stage: establishing that the estimated omitted element is this one, or not? (...) or another. The claim must be preceded by two stages: the first stage is establishing that there is an omission in the speech requiring explanation, and the second is establishing that the estimated element is this, meaning specifying the estimate; because even if we grant that the verse needs an estimate, it may be disputed, and it may be said to him: what is this estimate you have estimated? We do not grant that the estimate of the omitted element is this (...). Everyone who claims an omission in a verse needs two things or two stages: the first stage: establishing that there is an omission in the speech, and by what way do we know this? If the speech does not stand without an estimate, we know that there is an omission; this is one.

The second stage: establishing that the omitted element is this thing you estimated, since it is permissible that the estimate is something else, or not? And this is certainly an estimate determined by the context, because the context is what specifies the type of the omitted element.

Good, if the speech does not need this estimate, then it is better not to estimate. The meaning of this verse is very clear on the view of no estimate, and that the meaning is: We will make for you both authority by means of Our signs that are with you, so they will not reach you both; and this meaning is also clearer than what the author and others estimated, because in reality he says: ﴿with Our signs﴾ here is plural, and in the first he says: ﴿These two are proofs from your Lord to Pharaoh and his chiefs﴾ [al-Qasas 32]. So did Allah send them, when He sent them, with only one sign or with two signs? Two signs.

The correct view, then, is that the verse is connected, its parts joined to one another, and we read: ﴿so they will not reach you both with Our signs﴾, yes: ﴿And We will make for you both authority, so they will not reach you both with Our signs﴾, and it is attached to His saying: "We will make for you both authority with Our signs, so they will not reach you both."

Some of the grammarians claimed that His saying ﴿with Our signs﴾ is attached to ﴿the victorious﴾, and this in meaning is close to what we mentioned, meaning: "You two and whoever follows you are the victorious with Our signs." The one victorious by the signs is the one to whom authority was given through them, so on this view: "so they will not reach you both; you two and whoever follows you are the victorious with Our signs." Without doubt this is better than the author's estimate, because it needs no omission, and because it makes the speech connected in part to part; but there is an omission from the standpoint of grammatical rules, which is that ﴿the victorious﴾ is an active participle (ism fa'il), and the "al" attached to the active participle is, according to the grammarians, what? A relative pronoun:

"And a clear adjective, the ṣilah of (al) ..."

A relative pronoun, and it is known that a relative pronoun's complement does not operate on what precedes it; its complement does not govern, so we then need an answer to this rule.

The answer they gave: the "al" here is not relative, but like the "al" that enters on a fixed noun, entering on "the man" and "the lion" and similar.

So in this estimate there is a violation of the known grammatical rules.

We return now to the view that the correct approach is to make His saying ﴿with Our signs﴾ attached to ﴿And We will make for you both authority﴾, and we are spared all that: the violations, the estimates we rely on, and the specification of the estimated element.

And His saying ﴿with Our signs﴾, ﴿so they will not reach you both with Our signs﴾, contains evidence that Allah the Exalted gave Musa and Harun signs; and He mentioned in another surah that He gave him nine signs, or not? ﴿And We certainly gave Musa nine clear signs, so ask the Children of Israel when he came to them﴾ [al-Isra' 101].

And His saying ﴿you two and whoever follows you﴾: who are they? From the Children of Israel and from the family of Pharaoh, because among the family of Pharaoh were those who followed them, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And a believing man from the family of Pharaoh said﴾ [Ghafir 28].

And His saying ﴿and whoever follows you﴾ contains evidence that a person is aided and made victorious by following the messengers, and that there is no path to victory and dominance except entering the path of the messengers and following them. Accordingly, there is from this a rule: whoever is more closely following the Messenger is nearer to victory, and whoever is further from following the Messenger is further from victory; because it is known among the established rules that when a ruling is attached to an attribute, its establishment is in strength and weakness, existence and non-existence, according to that attribute. When a ruling is attached to an attribute, the establishment of the ruling is in existence and non-existence, strength and weakness, according to that attribute, understood?

For example: ﴿Indeed Allah is with the patient﴾ [al-Baqarah 153]: His companionship with the patient is in strength and weakness according to the patience they have.

﴿Indeed Allah is with those who are mindful of Him﴾ [al-Nahl 128]: the existence of companionship for the God-conscious is in strength and weakness according to their God-consciousness... and so on.

The Shaykh (Ibn 'Uthaymin) said, in his commentary on Allah's words:

﴿أَنْتُمَا وَمَنِ اتَّبَعَكُمَا الْغَالِبُونَ﴾ [al-Qasas 28:35] "You two and those who follow you will be the victors." **Al-ghalibun** (the victors): over whom? The author says: "(the victors) over them." ... But if we want to take this in its general sense, we say: ﴿أَنْتُمَا وَمَنِ اتَّبَعَكُمَا الْغَالِبُونَ﴾ means victorious over those who oppose them. The followers of the messengers are victorious over those who oppose the messengers, always and forever, or not? Always and forever. Indeed, these matters (...) over others. The Prophet ﷺ said: "I have been helped with terror (of my enemy) for a distance of one month."[[Agreed upon (Muttafaqun 'alayh). Al-Bukhari (438) and Muslim (521/3), from the hadith of Jabir ibn 'Abdullah, may Allah be pleased with him and his father.]] Allahu akbar! How great this benefit is, if only we were at the level we should be! If we truly followed this noble Prophet ﷺ in reality, our enemy would be terrified of us for a distance of one month. But, unfortunately, we were not truly following the Messenger, peace be upon him, in reality. Therefore our might has become between ourselves, neither those who claim Islam among us, nor those who wish to shelter under the principle of jahiliyyah, which is Arab nationalism (al-qawmiyyah al-'arabiyyah). Nationalism has not triumphed since its emergence until today, and it will never triumph. Rather, it only increases in failure, division and fragmentation, and indeed, fighting among its own. Likewise, in reality, we have not united on an Islamic nationality; we have not united on it. So the Muslims remain neither on this nor on that, and therefore we did not have the victory which Allah promised to His Prophet ﷺ.

He said: (﴿فَلَمَّا جَاءَهُمْ مُوسَى بِآيَاتِنَا بَيِّنَاتٍ﴾ [al-Qasas 28:36] clear, as a circumstantial state (hal)).

﴿فَلَمَّا جَاءَهُمْ﴾ means: the people of Pharaoh (Ali Fir'awn).

﴿مُوسَى بِآيَاتِنَا﴾: He did not say "and Harun," because the messengership originally belonged to Musa.

As for ﴿بِآيَاتِنَا﴾, the letter ba' indicates accompaniment, meaning accompanied by the signs.

﴿بِآيَاتِنَا﴾ is the plural of ayah, which means signs. It is attributed to Allah as the attribution of a gift to its giver, because these signs are not signs upon Allah; rather they are signs from Him, upon what? Upon the messengership of Musa, and Musa, within it, is proof that Allah alone is the true God.

﴿بِآيَاتِنَا بَيِّنَاتٍ﴾: He said "clear," and regarding its i'rab (grammatical analysis) he said: "a circumstantial state (hal)." A hal of what? (...)

Student: Of (ayat).

Shaykh: Of (ayat). And it is not correct to be an adjective (sifah)?

Student: (...)

Shaykh: Is it correct or not correct? Give me the ruling before the reason.

Student: It is not correct.

Shaykh: It is not correct, because (ayat) is definite (ma'rifah), and ﴿بَيِّنَاتٍ﴾ is indefinite (nakirah), and a definite noun is not described by an indefinite noun. Rather, when an indefinite noun comes after a definite noun and is its description, it is parsed as a hal.

In His words ﴿بِآيَاتِنَا بَيِّنَاتٍ﴾ there is an establishment of proof, because an ayah is a sign, and whenever it is more evident, the proof is stronger. So the signs are clear.
